```{r}
# Normalise okina/smart-quote variants so island-name joins are consistent
fix_island <- function(x) {
  x |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[ʻʼ'']", "'") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("ā", "a") |>   # for join matching only
    stringr::str_trim()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: theme-kona-paper

# Custom ggplot2 theme for all publication figures.
# Requirements: white bg, minimal grid, ~9pt text, no unnecessary legends,
# panel letters added via labs(tag = "A"), accessible palette,
# interpretable in grayscale.

theme_kona_paper <- function(base_size = 9, ...) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, ...) +
    theme(
      # Typography
      text              = element_text(colour = "gray10"),
      plot.title        = element_text(size = rel(1.15), face = "bold",
                                       margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = rel(0.95), colour = "gray40",
                                       margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.caption      = element_text(size = rel(0.82), colour = "gray50",
                                       hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 6)),
      plot.tag          = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.1)),
      # Axes
      axis.title        = element_text(size = rel(0.95)),
      axis.title.x      = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
      axis.title.y      = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
      axis.text         = element_text(size = rel(0.88), colour = "gray20"),
      axis.ticks        = element_line(colour = "gray70", linewidth = 0.3),
      # Panel
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "gray92", linewidth = 0.35),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.border      = element_blank(),
      # Facets
      strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "gray96", colour = NA),
      strip.text        = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.92)),
      # Legends
      legend.position   = "right",
      legend.title      = element_text(size = rel(0.9), face = "bold"),
      legend.text       = element_text(size = rel(0.85)),
      legend.key.size   = unit(0.9, "lines"),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
      # Margins
      plot.margin       = margin(8, 10, 6, 8)
    )
}

# Make it the default for this document
theme_set(theme_kona_paper())

# Helper: save a figure as both PDF (vector) and PNG (600 dpi)
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width, height,
                     dir = here("output", "main_figures")) {
  ggsave(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot,
         width = width, height = height, device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = 600)
  invisible(plot)
}

save_supp <- function(plot, name, width, height) {
  save_fig(plot, name, width, height,
           dir = here("output", "supplement"))
}
```

# Data Inventory and QA/QC {#sec-data-inventory}

> **Step 1.** Audit the sample data before doing any modeling.
> Target: explicit sample-flow table, site_id creation, coordinate QA.

```{r}
#| label: load-raw-chemistry

chem_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "clean_chemdata.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-spatial-support-files

ahupuaa   <- read_csv(here("data", "ahupuaa_cache.csv"),             show_col_types = FALSE)
cess_dist <- read_csv(here("data", "sample_cesspool_distances.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cess_buf  <- read_csv(here("data", "cesspool_buffer_counts.csv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
cess_ahu  <- read_csv(here("data", "cesspool_by_ahupuaa.csv"),       show_col_types = FALSE)
ccap      <- read_csv(here("data", "ccap_ahupuaa_summary.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
slope     <- read_csv(here("data", "ahupuaa_slope.csv"),             show_col_types = FALSE)
ksat      <- read_csv(here("data", "ahupuaa_ksat.csv"),              show_col_types = FALSE)
discharge <- read_csv(here("data", "usgs_discharge_march2026.csv"),  show_col_types = FALSE)
fetch     <- read_csv(here("data", "wave_fetch.csv"),                show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: resolve-duplicate-ahupuaa
# Several ahupuaa-level tables contain duplicate rows from multi-polygon
# boundary intersections during raster extraction. Resolved by averaging
# within the composite key ahupuaa + mokupuni (island).
#
# CRITICAL: ahupuaa names are NOT unique across islands. Seven names recur
# on multiple islands (Hālawa, Kahana, Kalihi, Kawela, Waiheʻe, Wailua, Waimea).
# All joins MUST use ahupuaa + mokupuni as a composite key.
# cesspool_by_ahupuaa uses column name 'island' (same encoding as mokupuni);
# rename to mokupuni before joining.

slope_clean <- slope |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(mean_slope_deg = mean(mean_slope_deg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ksat_clean <- ksat |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(mean_ksat_um_s = mean(mean_ksat_um_s, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ccap_clean <- ccap |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(
    pct_impervious  = mean(pct_impervious,  na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_agriculture = mean(pct_agriculture, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cess_ahu_clean <- cess_ahu |>
  rename(mokupuni = island) |>   # harmonise column name; encoding matches mokupuni
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(
    cesspool_density_per_km2 = mean(cesspool_density_per_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cesspools              = mean(n_cesspools,              na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

discharge_clean <- discharge |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(
    total_cfs_march            = mean(total_cfs_march,            na.rm = TRUE),
    specific_discharge_cfs_km2 = mean(specific_discharge_cfs_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) if_else(is.nan(x), NA_real_, x)))
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-coords-assign-site-id
# One sample has completely missing metadata (NA sample_id, island, coordinates).
# Drop it; all downstream analyses require coordinates.
has_coords <- chem_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))

# Assign a stable site_id: each unique lat/lon pair is one site.
# This is an exact-coordinate match — coordinates are already stored to ~5 dp.
site_lookup <- has_coords |>
  distinct(latitude, longitude) |>
  arrange(latitude, longitude) |>
  mutate(site_id = sprintf("SITE_%04d", row_number()))

chem_audit <- has_coords |>
  left_join(site_lookup, by = c("latitude", "longitude"))
```

*Table S1 (sample attrition) and Table S2 (missingness matrix) are generated after all
covariates are joined — see the end of [§ Master analytical dataset](#sec-master-dataset).*

```{r}
#| label: coordinate-duplicate-audit
# Classify the 33 multi-sample sites
site_type_tbl <- chem_audit |>
  group_by(site_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  summarise(
    n_samples  = n(),
    n_dates    = n_distinct(as.Date(collected_hst)),
    cv_NO3     = sd(NO3NO2, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(NO3NO2, na.rm = TRUE),
    cv_Si      = sd(SiO2,   na.rm = TRUE) / mean(SiO2,   na.rm = TRUE),
    site_type  = case_when(
      n_dates > 1                                                       ~ "same_site_repeat_visit",
      (is.na(cv_NO3) | cv_NO3 < 0.25) & (is.na(cv_Si) | cv_Si < 0.25) ~ "probable_technical_replicate",
      TRUE                                                              ~ "same_coord_independent_samples"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

site_type_tbl |>
  count(site_type, name = "n_sites") |>
  kable(caption = "Multi-sample sites by classification (33 sites share coordinates with ≥1 other sample).",
        col.names = c("Site type", "n sites")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Coordinate duplicate decisions.** Of 708 unique lat/lon positions, 33 have ≥2 samples.
Nine sites have nearly identical chemistry on the same date (probable technical replicates),
18 sites have substantially different chemistry on the same date (independent nearby
observations — retain all; shared coordinates may reflect GPS rounding),
and 6 sites have samples from different dates (genuine repeat visits).
All 746 samples are retained for nutrient-specific analyses; hierarchical random effects
(site nested in ahupuaʻa nested in island) will account for pseudoreplication in
landscape-scale models.
:::

```{r}
#| label: build-master-dataset
# Build one-row-per-sample master dataset with all covariates joined.
# This is the base for all downstream analyses.

chem_master <- chem_audit |>
  left_join(ahupuaa |> select(sample_id, ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni),
            by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(cess_dist,                                          by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(cess_buf,                                           by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(fetch |> select(sample_id, fetch_mean_km, fetch_min_km),
            by = "sample_id") |>
  # All ahupuaa-level joins use composite key ahupuaa + mokupuni to prevent
  # cross-island name collisions (7 ahupuaa names recur on multiple islands)
  left_join(slope_clean,    by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni")) |>
  left_join(ksat_clean,     by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni")) |>
  left_join(ccap_clean,     by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni")) |>
  left_join(cess_ahu_clean  |> select(ahupuaa, mokupuni, cesspool_density_per_km2, n_cesspools),
            by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni")) |>
  left_join(discharge_clean |> select(ahupuaa, mokupuni, total_cfs_march, specific_discharge_cfs_km2),
            by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni"))

# site_lookup saved here; chem_master saved after BDL substitution and cesspool correction
write_csv(site_lookup, here("data", "site_lookup.csv"))
```



::: {.callout-warning}
**Key data gaps to note before modeling.**

- **USGS stream discharge** (61.5% missing): **this is gauge-coverage missingness, not
  streamlessness.** Of the 470 ungauged samples, 91% (n = 426) are within 5 km of an
  OSM stream mouth, and median distance to the nearest stream mouth is ≤ 0.5 km on
  Maui, Molokaʻi, and Lānaʻi. USGS gauges exist only for major perennial streams; the
  many smaller coastal drainages that were sampled are simply ungauged. Treating missing
  discharge as zero would be scientifically incorrect. Use `dist_to_stream_mouth_m`
  (computed from OSM stream mouths; now in `chem_master`) as the primary within-watershed
  connectivity variable; use spatially resolved CHIRPS storm rainfall as the storm-forcing
  variable. Reserve USGS discharge for sensitivity analysis and supplementary context.
- **NH₄** (18.5% missing): missingness is distributed across islands; NH₄-specific models
  will use a smaller sample. Do not impute; report n separately.
- **Cesspool metrics — island-specific data coverage** (updated 2026-09-10).
  • **Oʻahu, Maui:** HCPT layer 32 (Hawaiʻi Statewide GIS, current inventory). Full ahupuaʻa and sample-level coverage.
  • **Molokaʻi:** DOH OSDS layer (2010 vintage, 417 Class I systems, 38 ahupuaʻa). All 103 Molokaʻi 
    samples have complete sample-level metrics; ahupuaʻa-level metrics available for 93/103 samples 
    (90.3% coverage). **Comparability caveat:** Different data source and vintage (2010 vs. current) 
    may affect cross-island magnitude comparisons. Recommend reporting sensitivity analyses with/without 
    Molokaʻi to assess robustness.
  • **Lānaʻi:** No cesspool layer available. Buffer counts correctly 0 (no on-island cesspools in HCPT 
    layer). Distance-to-nearest is `NA` for all samples (sample-level distances 16–34 km reference 
    off-island sources). An earlier observation of "9 cesspools in Kamoku (Lānaʻi)" was a cross-island 
    join artefact: those records belong to Kamoku on Hawaiʻi Island; the composite-key fix eliminated this.
:::

```{r}
#| label: bdl-substitution
# All reported zeros are below-detection-limit (BDL), not true zeros.
# Substitution rule: replace with DL/2 where DL = minimum observed non-zero value.
# BDL indicator columns (bdl_*) retain the original flag for sensitivity analyses.

dl_half <- c(
  NO3NO2 = min(chem_master$NO3NO2[chem_master$NO3NO2 > 0], na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
  PO4    = min(chem_master$PO4[chem_master$PO4 > 0],       na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
  NH3    = min(chem_master$NH3[chem_master$NH3 > 0],       na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
  SiO2   = min(chem_master$SiO2[chem_master$SiO2 > 0],     na.rm = TRUE) / 2
)

chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    bdl_NO3NO2 = !is.na(NO3NO2) & NO3NO2 == 0,
    bdl_PO4    = !is.na(PO4)    & PO4    == 0,
    bdl_NH3    = !is.na(NH3)    & NH3    == 0,
    bdl_SiO2   = !is.na(SiO2)  & SiO2   == 0,
    NO3NO2 = if_else(bdl_NO3NO2, dl_half["NO3NO2"], NO3NO2),
    PO4    = if_else(bdl_PO4,    dl_half["PO4"],    PO4),
    NH3    = if_else(bdl_NH3,    dl_half["NH3"],     NH3),
    SiO2   = if_else(bdl_SiO2,  dl_half["SiO2"],    SiO2)
  )

# Summary table
bdl_tbl <- tibble(
  Nutrient    = c("NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084", "SiO\u2082"),
  n_bdl       = c(sum(chem_master$bdl_NO3NO2), sum(chem_master$bdl_PO4),
                  sum(chem_master$bdl_NH3),    sum(chem_master$bdl_SiO2)),
  n_available = c(sum(!is.na(chem_master$NO3NO2)), sum(!is.na(chem_master$PO4)),
                  sum(!is.na(chem_master$NH3)),     sum(!is.na(chem_master$SiO2))),
  pct_bdl     = round(100 * n_bdl / n_available, 1),
  `DL/2 substituted (umol/L)` = round(dl_half, 4)
)

bdl_tbl |>
  kable(caption = "BDL substitution summary. All zeros replaced with DL/2 (half the minimum observed non-zero value). BDL flags retained in `bdl_*` columns for sensitivity analyses.",
        align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**NH₄ has 30.4% BDL observations.** DL/2 substitution is defensible for modest BDL fractions,
but at 30% the substituted values can meaningfully inflate apparent precision.
The NH₄ model should be treated as a candidate for censored regression (e.g., `survival::Surv`
left-censored, or a Bayesian truncated-normal likelihood in `brms`). A sensitivity analysis
comparing DL/2 results to a censored model is required for any inferential claim about NH₄.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cesspool-island-corrections
# Molokaʻi: HCPT layer 32 has no coverage — all cesspool metrics set to NA.
# Lānaʻi: no on-island cesspools in the layer for most ahupuaʻa; buffer counts
# and density are correctly 0 where present, but dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m
# values (16–34 km) reference off-island sources and are set to NA.
# Molokaʻi: layer does not cover island → all cesspool metrics NA.
# Lānaʻi: island absent from cesspool_by_ahupuaa → density NA.
#   dist_to_nearest set to NA (sample-level values pointed off-island, 16–34 km).
#   Buffer counts correctly 0 (no on-island cesspools in HCPT layer).
#   The earlier "Kamoku 9-cesspool" flag was a cross-island join artefact
#   (Hawaiʻi Island's Kamoku); resolved by the composite ahupuaa+mokupuni key.
# Molokaʻi: UPDATED 2026-09-10 — cesspool data now available from DOH OSDS 2010 inventory.
#   Keep Molokaʻi cesspool metrics (no longer NA). Different data source/vintage than HCPT.
#   See comparability caveat in Step 12.
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    # Keep Molokaʻi cesspool data (now integrated from DOH OSDS 2010 inventory)
    # Lānaʻi: no meaningful cesspool distances (references off-island cesspools)
    dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m = if_else(grepl("n.?a.?i", island, ignore.case = TRUE),
                                          NA_real_, dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: dist-to-stream-mouth
# Compute distance from each sample to the nearest OSM stream mouth.
# Source: osm_stream_mouths.csv (OpenStreetMap, filtered to 400 m coastal buffer).
# Missing discharge data reflects gauge-coverage gaps, not absent streams:
# 91% of ungauged samples are within 5 km of a mapped stream mouth.
# dist_to_stream_mouth_m is therefore the primary connectivity variable.

stream_mouths <- read_csv(here("data", "osm_stream_mouths.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

samples_sf <- chem_master |>
  select(sample_id, latitude, longitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)   # UTM zone 4N

streams_sf <- stream_mouths |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(samples_sf, streams_sf)
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(dist_to_stream_mouth_m = as.numeric(
    st_distance(samples_sf, streams_sf[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
  ))
```

```{r}
#| label: offshore-flags
# Flag samples that fall outside the stream-connectivity framework.
# offshore_reference: samples in the "Open Ocean" ahupuaa — deliberately
#   collected far offshore as marine background (n = 11; 15–114 km from
#   any stream mouth). Exclude from connectivity and landscape models;
#   retain as marine background context.
# far_from_stream: dist_to_stream_mouth_m > 10 km (n = 35 total).
#   Includes the 11 offshore reference samples plus 24 leeward O'ahu
#   coastal samples (Honouliuli, Nānākuli, Waiʻanae, Waipiʻo ahupuaʻa)
#   in genuinely stream-sparse dry terrain. Leeward samples retain
#   valid CHIRPS land-pixel data and are kept in landscape models with
#   the caveat that stream-proximity effects are poorly constrained there.

chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    offshore_reference = ahupuaa == "Open Ocean",
    far_from_stream    = dist_to_stream_mouth_m > 10000
  )

# CHIRPS -9999 fill values indicate ocean/off-land pixels — same set as offshore samples.
# These receive NA for all CHIRPS metrics.
```

```{r}
#| label: chirps-storm-rainfall
# Step 5 — Spatially resolved CHIRPS storm rainfall metrics.
# Source: CHC server (data.chc.ucsb.edu), 0.05° (~5 km) daily resolution,
#   March 10–31 2026. Cached to data/chirps_march2026_daily_raw.rds.
# Fill value -9999 (ocean pixels) → NA.
# April 1–8 data unavailable from CHC; post-storm April rainfall was near-zero
#   (0–2.4 mm/day), so Mar 10–31 cumulative captures effectively all storm rainfall.
# Metrics computed (Step 5 complete):
#   chirps_storm_cumulative_mm — Mar 10–31 total (primary event-exposure variable)
#   chirps_peak_day_mm         — maximum single-day rainfall
#   chirps_3day_max_mm         — maximum rolling 3-day sum
#   chirps_7day_mm             — 7-day core storm total (Mar 10–16)
#   chirps_storm_days_nonzero  — number of rain days
#   chirps_peak_date           — date of maximum daily rainfall
#   chirps_days_since_peak     — days from pixel peak to sample collection

chirps_march_all <- readRDS(here("data", "chirps_march2026_daily_raw.rds"))

unique_locs <- chem_master |>
  mutate(chirps_lon = round(longitude, 2), chirps_lat = round(latitude, 2)) |>
  distinct(chirps_lon, chirps_lat) |>
  arrange(chirps_lat, chirps_lon) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

chirps_daily <- as_tibble(chirps_march_all) |>
  left_join(unique_locs, by = "id") |>
  mutate(chirps = if_else(chirps == -9999, NA_real_, chirps)) |>
  arrange(chirps_lon, chirps_lat, date)

# Per-pixel summary metrics
chirps_pixel <- chirps_daily |>
  group_by(chirps_lon, chirps_lat) |>
  mutate(roll3 = slider::slide_dbl(chirps, sum, .before = 2, .after = 0,
                                   .complete = TRUE, na_rm = TRUE)) |>
  summarise(
    chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = sum(chirps, na.rm = TRUE),
    chirps_peak_day_mm         = max(chirps, na.rm = TRUE),
    chirps_3day_max_mm         = max(roll3,  na.rm = TRUE),
    chirps_7day_mm             = sum(chirps[date >= as.Date("2026-03-10") &
                                            date <= as.Date("2026-03-16")],
                                     na.rm = TRUE),
    chirps_storm_days_nonzero  = sum(chirps > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    chirps_ocean_pixel         = any(is.na(chirps)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(chirps_storm_cumulative_mm, chirps_peak_day_mm,
                  chirps_3day_max_mm, chirps_7day_mm),
                \(x) if_else(chirps_ocean_pixel | is.infinite(x), NA_real_, x)))

# Peak date per pixel (separate to avoid ties issue in summarise)
chirps_peak_date_df <- chirps_daily |>
  filter(!is.na(chirps)) |>
  group_by(chirps_lon, chirps_lat) |>
  slice_max(chirps, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(chirps_lon, chirps_lat, chirps_peak_date = date) |>
  ungroup()

chirps_pixel <- chirps_pixel |>
  left_join(chirps_peak_date_df, by = c("chirps_lon", "chirps_lat"))

# Join all metrics to chem_master
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(chirps_lon = round(longitude, 2), chirps_lat = round(latitude, 2)) |>
  left_join(chirps_pixel, by = c("chirps_lon", "chirps_lat")) |>
  mutate(chirps_days_since_peak = as.integer(
    as.Date(collected_hst) - chirps_peak_date
  ))
```


# Sampling Coverage {#sec-sampling-coverage}

> **Step 6 (Figure 1).** Four-island map, event timeline, summary statistics.
> Show the scale of the natural experiment — do not show nutrient concentrations yet.

```{r}
#| label: fig1-sampling-map
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Sampling design and storm context. Four Hawaiian islands (Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi) showing all unique coastal sampling sites (filled circles, coloured by island) and stream mouths (open white triangles, drawn on top; OpenStreetMap). Scale bars at bottom-left of each map panel. Pacific inset shows archipelago context. Bottom panels show 4-island mean daily rainfall (NCEP GDAS, upper) and daily discharge at three USGS key gauges (lower, log₁₀ scale) for March–April 2026 with aligned x-axes. All three gauges peaked March 13–14. Basemap: Esri World Imagery."

STREAM_COL <- "#00ACC1"   # bright teal — distinct from all island colours and satellite imagery

normalize_apos <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "[\u2018\u2019\u02bc\u0027]", "'")

# ── Satellite tile cache (downloaded once, reused on render) ──────────────────
tile_dir <- here("data", "maptiles_cache")
dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

island_bbox <- list(
  "O'ahu"    = c(xmin=-158.33, xmax=-157.60, ymin=21.22, ymax=21.73),
  "Maui"     = c(xmin=-156.72, xmax=-155.95, ymin=20.50, ymax=21.05),
  "Moloka'i" = c(xmin=-157.38, xmax=-156.68, ymin=21.02, ymax=21.27),
  "Lāna'i"   = c(xmin=-157.08, xmax=-156.72, ymin=20.71, ymax=20.97)
)
zoom_levels <- c("O'ahu"=11, "Maui"=11, "Moloka'i"=12, "Lāna'i"=12)

make_bbox_sf <- function(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
  st_bbox(c(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax), crs=4326) |>
  st_as_sfc()

# terra SpatRasters don't safely deserialise from RDS across sessions.
# get_tiles() uses its own file cache (tile_dir) — no re-download after first render.
tiles <- imap(island_bbox, \(bb, isl)
  get_tiles(
    st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin=unname(bb["xmin"]), xmax=unname(bb["xmax"]),
                         ymin=unname(bb["ymin"]), ymax=unname(bb["ymax"])),
                       crs=4326)),
    provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
    zoom     = zoom_levels[[isl]],
    cachedir = tile_dir
  )
)

# ── Sample sites and stream mouths ────────────────────────────────────────────
samples_plot <- chem_master |>
  dplyr::filter(!offshore_reference) |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(sample_id, island, latitude, longitude)

stream_mouths_plot <- read_csv(here("data", "osm_stream_mouths.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(island %in% c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i", "Lāna'i"))

island_pal_norm <- island_pal
names(island_pal_norm) <- normalize_apos(names(island_pal_norm))

island_counts_norm <- chem_master |>
  dplyr::filter(!offshore_reference) |>
  mutate(island_n = normalize_apos(island)) |>
  count(island_n, name = "n_samples")

# ── Island panel: satellite + scale bar, label at top ────────────────────────
make_sat_panel <- function(isl) {
  isl_n <- normalize_apos(isl)
  bb    <- island_bbox[[isl]]
  pts   <- samples_plot       |> dplyr::filter(normalize_apos(island) == isl_n)
  strm  <- stream_mouths_plot |> dplyr::filter(normalize_apos(island) == isl_n)
  ns    <- island_counts_norm$n_samples[island_counts_norm$island_n == isl_n]
  col   <- island_pal_norm[[isl_n]]
  lbl_x <- mean(c(bb["xmin"], bb["xmax"]))
  lbl_y <- bb["ymax"] - 0.06 * (bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"])   # top of panel
  hw    <- (bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"]) * 0.40

  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster_rgb(data = tiles[[isl]]) +
    # Stream mouths FIRST (below) — solid teal, visible through sample points
    geom_point(data = strm, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude),
               shape = 24, size = 1.5, stroke = 0.5,
               fill = STREAM_COL, colour = "white", alpha = 0.80) +
    # Sample sites ON TOP — island colour, semi-transparent so teal shows through
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude),
               shape = 21, size = 1.8, stroke = 0.3,
               fill = col, colour = "white", alpha = 0.60) +
    annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.28,
                     text_col = "white", bar_cols = c("white", "gray40"),
                     line_col = "white", text_cex = 0.65,
                     pad_x = unit(0.08, "in"), pad_y = unit(0.08, "in")) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(bb["xmin"], bb["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(bb["ymin"], bb["ymax"]),
             expand = FALSE, crs = 4326) +
    # Semi-transparent white label pill at top (readable on satellite)
    annotate("rect",
             xmin = lbl_x - hw, xmax = lbl_x + hw,
             ymin = lbl_y - 0.018, ymax = lbl_y + 0.009,
             fill = alpha("white", 0.78), colour = NA) +
    annotate("text", x = lbl_x, y = lbl_y,
             label = sprintf("%s  (n = %d)", isl, ns),
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", colour = col) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.border    = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "gray50", linewidth = 0.4)
    )
}

# ── Pacific inset (light, print-friendly) ────────────────────────────────────
p_inset <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf"),
          fill = "gray80", colour = "gray55", linewidth = 0.15) +
  annotate("point", x = -157.8, y = 21.3, shape = 23,
           fill = "#C62828", colour = "white", size = 2.8, stroke = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-210, -100), ylim = c(-10, 60), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#D6EAF8", colour = "gray60",
                                       linewidth = 0.5))

# ── Shared timeline theme (white, print-ready) ────────────────────────────────
theme_tl <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(
      plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "gray88", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text          = element_text(colour = "gray20", size = 7),
      axis.title.y       = element_text(colour = "gray20", size = 7.5,
                                        margin = margin(r = 4))
    )
}

  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-03-16"), y = 1040,

  nrow(chem_master |> dplyr::filter(!offshore_reference)),

  plot_layout(widths = c(2.2, 1.3, 1.8, 1.7))

fig1 <- (top_row / mid_row / p_timeline) +

    theme   = theme(

suppressWarnings(fig1)
```

# Event Magnitude and Long-Term Context {#sec-event-magnitude}

## Nutrient enrichment — storm vs background {#sec-enrichment}

> **Step 7 (Figure 2).** Quantify the magnitude of nutrient enrichment.
> Four-panel: NO₃+NO₂, PO₄, NH₄, Si — storm-influenced vs marine-background.

```{r}
#| label: step7-salinity-groups

# Salinity threshold: marine background > 34 PSU (unaffected Hawaiian coastal water);
# storm-influenced ≤ 34 PSU (any freshwater dilution signal). No samples excluded.
fig2_df <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    sal_group = if_else(Salinity > 34, "Marine background", "Storm-influenced"),
    sal_group = factor(sal_group, levels = c("Storm-influenced", "Marine background"))
  )

# Sample sizes per group per nutrient
fig2_df |>
  group_by(sal_group) |>
  summarise(
    n_samples = n(),
    n_NO3NO2  = sum(!is.na(NO3NO2)),
    n_PO4     = sum(!is.na(PO4)),
    n_NH3     = sum(!is.na(NH3)),
    n_SiO2    = sum(!is.na(SiO2))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Samples per salinity group entering Figure 2.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step7-bootstrap-fold

# Bootstrap median fold enrichment: median(storm) / median(background)
# 4,999 replicates; 95% percentile CI.
set.seed(2847)

boot_fold <- function(df, col, n_boot = 4999) {
  storm <- df |> filter(sal_group == "Storm-influenced") |>
    pull({{ col }}) |> na.omit()
  bg    <- df |> filter(sal_group == "Marine background") |>
    pull({{ col }}) |> na.omit()
  obs   <- median(storm) / median(bg)
  ci    <- replicate(n_boot, {
    median(sample(storm, replace = TRUE)) / median(sample(bg, replace = TRUE))
  })
  tibble(
    fold    = obs,
    lo95    = quantile(ci, 0.025),
    hi95    = quantile(ci, 0.975),
    n_storm = length(storm),
    n_bg    = length(bg)
  )
}

fold_results <- bind_rows(
  boot_fold(fig2_df, NO3NO2) |> mutate(nutrient_f = "NO[3]+NO[2]"),
  boot_fold(fig2_df, PO4)    |> mutate(nutrient_f = "PO[4]"),
  boot_fold(fig2_df, NH3)    |> mutate(nutrient_f = "NH[4]"),
  boot_fold(fig2_df, SiO2)   |> mutate(nutrient_f = "SiO[2]")
)

fold_results |>
  mutate(across(c(fold, lo95, hi95), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  select(nutrient_f, fold, lo95, hi95, n_storm, n_bg) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Nutrient", "Fold", "95% CI lo", "95% CI hi", "n storm", "n background"),
    caption   = "Median fold enrichment (storm / marine background) with 95% bootstrap CI."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig2-nutrient-distributions
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**Figure 2.** Coastal nutrient concentrations split by salinity group: storm-influenced (Sal ≤ 34 PSU; orange) and marine background (Sal > 34 PSU; blue). Each point is one sample (jittered); violins show the empirical distribution; bold crossbar is the median. Fold-enrichment annotation shows median(storm)/median(background) [95% bootstrap CI, n = 4,999 replicates]. BDL samples excluded from plot (NO₃+NO₂: n = 44; PO₄: n = 77; NH₄: n = 185; SiO₂: n = 27); medians are well above detection limits so fold-enrichment estimates are unaffected."

# Factor levels for nutrient facets
nutrient_lvls <- c("NO[3]+NO[2]", "PO[4]", "NH[4]", "SiO[2]")

# Long format — one row per sample × nutrient.
# BDL values are set to NA before pivoting: they sit at a fixed detection-limit
# floor (NO3NO2 = 0.03, PO4 = 0.003, NH4 = 0.04, SiO2 = 0.005 umol/L) and
# create an artificial cluster near zero on the log scale.
# Medians are well above the detection limit in both groups, so removal does
# not affect the fold-enrichment estimates.
fig2_long <- fig2_df |>
  mutate(
    NO3NO2 = if_else(bdl_NO3NO2, NA_real_, NO3NO2),
    PO4    = if_else(bdl_PO4,    NA_real_, PO4),
    NH3    = if_else(bdl_NH3,    NA_real_, NH3),
    SiO2   = if_else(bdl_SiO2,   NA_real_, SiO2)
  ) |>
  select(sample_id, sal_group, island, NO3NO2, PO4, NH3, SiO2) |>
  pivot_longer(c(NO3NO2, PO4, NH3, SiO2),
               names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(
    nutrient_f = factor(nutrient,
                        levels = c("NO3NO2", "PO4", "NH3", "SiO2"),
                        labels = nutrient_lvls)
  )

# Fold-enrichment labels, centered between groups (x = 1.5 on discrete axis)
fold_annot <- fold_results |>
  mutate(
    nutrient_f = factor(nutrient_f, levels = nutrient_lvls),
    label      = sprintf("%.1f\u00D7  [%.1f\u2013%.1f]", fold, lo95, hi95)
  )

# Group colours — Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe
grp_cols <- c("Storm-influenced" = "#D55E00", "Marine background" = "#0072B2")

ggplot(fig2_long, aes(x = sal_group, y = conc,
                      fill = sal_group, colour = sal_group)) +
  # Distribution
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.18, linewidth = 0.35, width = 0.75) +
  # Individual samples
  geom_jitter(width = 0.08, alpha = 0.28, size = 0.75, stroke = 0) +
  # Median crossbar
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar",
               width = 0.42, linewidth = 0.6, fatten = NULL,
               colour = "gray10", fill = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Fold-enrichment annotation
  geom_text(
    data        = fold_annot,
    aes(label   = label),
    x           = 1.5,
    y           = Inf,
    vjust       = 1.5,
    size        = 2.7,
    colour      = "gray20",
    fontface    = "bold",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient_f, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1,
             labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_y_log10(
    labels = \(x) formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 2)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = grp_cols,
    labels = c("Storm-influenced (Sal \u2264 34)", "Marine background (Sal > 34)")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = grp_cols,
    labels = c("Storm-influenced (Sal \u2264 34)", "Marine background (Sal > 34)")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Storm", "Marine")) +
  labs(
    x      = NULL,
    y      = expression(Concentration~(µmol~L^{-1})),
    fill   = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  # Note: x-axis "Storm" = Sal ≤ 34 PSU (all freshwater-diluted samples);
  #       "Marine" = Sal > 34 PSU (unaffected coastal water). No samples excluded.
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 9.5),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 8)
  ) +
  guides(
    fill   = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.5, size = 3)),
    colour = "none"
  )
```

## Long-term Hui baseline comparison {#sec-hui-baseline}

> **Step 8.** Load Hui o Ka Wai Ola data, compute station-specific historical baselines,
> calculate fold-changes relative to pre-2026 medians.

```{r}
#| label: step8-load-hui

# Read both Hui files with explicit NA strings to handle #N/A cells
hui_s_raw <- read_excel(
  here("data/background_nutrients/hui-south-maui-thru-2026-1st-quarter.0.xlsx"),
  sheet = "data", na = c("", "NA", "#N/A")
)
hui_w_raw <- read_excel(
  here("data/background_nutrients/hui-west-maui-thru-2026-1st-quarter.0.xlsx"),
  sheet = "data", na = c("", "NA", "#N/A")
)

# Combine; coerce any remaining character columns to numeric
hui_raw <- bind_rows(
  hui_s_raw |> mutate(coast = "south"),
  hui_w_raw |> mutate(coast = "west")
) |>
  mutate(across(c(Turbidity, NNN, Phosphate, Silicate, NH4), as.numeric))

cat("Combined Hui: n =", nrow(hui_raw),
    "| stations:", n_distinct(hui_raw$Station),
    "| dates:", format(min(hui_raw$Date), "%Y-%m"),
    "to", format(max(hui_raw$Date), "%Y-%m"), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step8-clean-convert

# Unit conversions (µg/L → µmol/L) per AGENTS.md:
#   NNN  ÷ 14.007  (µg N/L → µmol/L)
#   NH4  ÷ 14.007  (µg N/L → µmol/L)
#   Phosphate ÷ 30.974 (µg P/L → µmol/L)
#   Silicate  ÷ 28.086 (µg Si/L → µmol/L)
hui <- hui_raw |>
  select(coast, Station, SiteName, Date, Lat, Long,
         NNN, Phosphate, Silicate, NH4) |>
  mutate(
    year        = year(Date),
    month       = month(Date),
    ym          = floor_date(Date, "month"),
    NO3NO2_umol = NNN       / 14.007,
    PO4_umol    = Phosphate / 30.974,
    SiO2_umol   = Silicate  / 28.086,
    NH3_umol    = NH4       / 14.007
  )

# Missingness per nutrient
hui |>
  summarise(across(c(NO3NO2_umol, PO4_umol, SiO2_umol, NH3_umol),
                   \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Missing values per nutrient after unit conversion.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step8-baselines

# Station-specific historical baselines: pre-2026 median per station per nutrient.
# Require ≥ 6 pre-2026 observations per station to include in fold-change calculation.
MIN_HIST_N <- 6

hui_hist <- hui |>
  filter(year < 2026) |>
  group_by(Station, coast) |>
  summarise(
    n_hist          = n(),
    hist_NO3NO2     = if (sum(!is.na(NO3NO2_umol)) >= MIN_HIST_N) median(NO3NO2_umol, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    hist_PO4        = if (sum(!is.na(PO4_umol))    >= MIN_HIST_N) median(PO4_umol,    na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    hist_SiO2       = if (sum(!is.na(SiO2_umol))   >= MIN_HIST_N) median(SiO2_umol,   na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    hist_NH3        = if (sum(!is.na(NH3_umol))     >= MIN_HIST_N) median(NH3_umol,    na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Stations with adequate history (n_hist ≥", MIN_HIST_N, "):",
    sum(hui_hist$n_hist >= MIN_HIST_N), "of", nrow(hui_hist), "\n")
cat("Stations qualifying per nutrient:\n")
hui_hist |>
  summarise(
    NO3NO2 = sum(!is.na(hist_NO3NO2)),
    PO4    = sum(!is.na(hist_PO4)),
    SiO2   = sum(!is.na(hist_SiO2)),
    NH3    = sum(!is.na(hist_NH3))
  ) |>
  print()
```

```{r}
#| label: step8-fold-changes

# Join baselines back and compute fold changes for every observation (all years)
hui_fc <- hui |>
  left_join(hui_hist |> select(-n_hist), by = c("Station", "coast")) |>
  mutate(
    fc_NO3NO2 = NO3NO2_umol / hist_NO3NO2,
    fc_PO4    = PO4_umol    / hist_PO4,
    fc_SiO2   = SiO2_umol   / hist_SiO2,
    fc_NH3    = NH3_umol    / hist_NH3
  )

# Monthly median fold change across all qualifying stations
hui_monthly <- hui_fc |>
  group_by(year, month, ym) |>
  summarise(
    n_stations    = n_distinct(Station),
    fc_NO3NO2_med = median(fc_NO3NO2, na.rm = TRUE),
    fc_PO4_med    = median(fc_PO4,    na.rm = TRUE),
    fc_SiO2_med   = median(fc_SiO2,   na.rm = TRUE),
    fc_NH3_med    = median(fc_NH3,    na.rm = TRUE),
    # raw medians for context
    NO3NO2_med    = median(NO3NO2_umol, na.rm = TRUE),
    PO4_med       = median(PO4_umol,    na.rm = TRUE),
    SiO2_med      = median(SiO2_umol,   na.rm = TRUE),
    NH3_med       = median(NH3_umol,    na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join CHIRPS monthly rainfall
chirps_monthly <- read_csv(here("data/chirps_maui_monthly_full.csv"),
                            show_col_types = FALSE)

hui_chirps <- hui_monthly |>
  left_join(chirps_monthly |> select(ym, chirps_mm), by = "ym")

# Snapshot of March 2026 vs overall medians
hui_chirps |>
  filter(year == 2026, month == 3) |>
  select(ym, n_stations, chirps_mm,
         fc_NO3NO2_med, fc_PO4_med, fc_SiO2_med, fc_NH3_med) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "March 2026 monthly station-median fold changes vs station historical medians.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step8-context-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "**Step 8 context.** Top: Monthly Maui island-mean rainfall (CHIRPS, Jun 2016–Mar 2026). March 2026 (373 mm) is the highest month on record — more than 2× the second-wettest March (2021, 165 mm). Bottom: Hui o Ka Wai Ola station-median fold change relative to site-specific historical medians (pre-2026) for NO₃+NO₂ and SiO₂. Points = monthly values (n stations shown in top panel); orange triangle = March 2026. Fold change = 1 (dashed) indicates no departure from baseline."

# Coerce ym to Date for consistent axis scaling
chirps_plot <- chirps_monthly |>
  mutate(is_storm = (year == 2026 & month == 3),
         ym = as.Date(ym))

hui_plot <- hui_chirps |>
  filter(!is.na(fc_NO3NO2_med)) |>
  mutate(is_storm = (year == 2026 & month == 3),
         ym = as.Date(ym))

# ── Panel A: rainfall time series ─────────────────────────────────────────────
pA_hui <- ggplot(chirps_plot, aes(x = ym, y = chirps_mm)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = is_storm), width = 27, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray72", "TRUE" = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y",
               expand = expansion(add = 20)) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-03-01"), y = 373,
           label = "Mar 2026\n373 mm", vjust = -0.25, hjust = 0.5,
           size = 2.7, colour = "#D55E00", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Rainfall (mm/month)", tag = "A") +
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 9)

# ── Panel B: fold-change time series for NO3NO2 and SiO2 ─────────────────────
hui_fc_long <- hui_plot |>
  select(ym, is_storm,
         `NO[3]+NO[2]` = fc_NO3NO2_med,
         `SiO[2]`      = fc_SiO2_med) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`NO[3]+NO[2]`, `SiO[2]`),
               names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "fold_change") |>
  mutate(nutrient = factor(nutrient, levels = c("NO[3]+NO[2]", "SiO[2]")))

pB_hui <- ggplot(hui_fc_long, aes(x = ym, y = fold_change, colour = nutrient)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.35, colour = "gray55") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, !is_storm), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is_storm),
             shape = 17, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient, nrow = 1, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("NO[3]+NO[2]" = "#1565C0", "SiO[2]" = "#2E7D32"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y",
               expand = expansion(add = 20)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fold change\n(monthly median / station baseline)", tag = "B") +
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 9)

pA_hui / pB_hui + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.1))
```

## Was 2026 statistically extreme? {#sec-extreme-test}

> **Step 9 (Figure 3).** Test whether March 2026 anomalies exceed the range expected
> from the decade-long rainfall–nutrient relationship.

```{r}
#| label: step9-station-level-mar26

# Station-level fold changes in March 2026 — the network median masks large
# variation. 47 stations sampled; we inspect which were most impacted.
hui_mar26 <- hui_fc |>
  filter(year == 2026, month == 3)

# Distribution across stations
cat("March 2026 station-level fold change distribution (n = 47 stations):\n")
hui_mar26 |>
  summarise(across(c(fc_NO3NO2, fc_PO4, fc_SiO2, fc_NH3),
    list(
      n      = \(x) sum(!is.na(x)),
      median = \(x) round(median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      p90    = \(x) round(quantile(x, .90, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      max    = \(x) round(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      pct_gt3x = \(x) round(mean(x > 3, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 0)
    )
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = c("nutrient", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.+)_(n|median|p90|max|pct_gt3x)") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Station-level NO₃+NO₂, PO₄, SiO₂, NH₄ fold enrichment in March 2026 relative to site-specific historical medians.")

# Top 10 stations by NO3+NO2 fold change
cat("\nTop 10 stations — NO₃+NO₂:\n")
hui_mar26 |>
  filter(!is.na(fc_NO3NO2)) |>
  arrange(desc(fc_NO3NO2)) |>
  select(Station, SiteName, coast, fc_NO3NO2, NO3NO2_umol) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Station", "Site", "Coast", "Fold change", "NO₃+NO₂ (µmol/L)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: step9-regression-setup

# Monthly fold-change dataset for regression: exclude March 2026 from fitting.
# Use log-log model (log fc ~ log rainfall) — best AIC across all nutrients.
reg_df <- hui_chirps |>
  filter(!is.na(fc_NO3NO2_med), !is.na(chirps_mm)) |>
  filter(!(year == 2026 & month == 3)) |>
  mutate(log_rain = log(chirps_mm))

# Fit log-log models for NO3NO2, PO4, SiO2, NH3
m_N  <- lm(log(fc_NO3NO2_med) ~ log_rain, data = reg_df)
m_P  <- lm(log(fc_PO4_med)    ~ log_rain, data = reg_df)
m_Si <- lm(log(fc_SiO2_med)   ~ log_rain, data = reg_df)
m_NH <- lm(log(fc_NH3_med)    ~ log_rain, data = reg_df)

# Model comparison (AIC was also compared against linear and log-predictor models)
cat("AIC — log(fc) ~ log(rain), all nutrients:\n")
AIC(m_N, m_P, m_Si, m_NH)

cat("\nModel coefficients (slope = elasticity: % change fc per % change rain):\n")
map_dfr(list(NO3NO2 = m_N, PO4 = m_P, SiO2 = m_Si, NH3 = m_NH),
        \(m) tibble(
          slope  = coef(m)[["log_rain"]],
          se     = sqrt(vcov(m)["log_rain", "log_rain"]),
          p      = summary(m)$coefficients["log_rain", "Pr(>|t|)"],
          r2     = summary(m)$r.squared
        ),
        .id = "nutrient") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Log-log regression of monthly median fold change on monthly CHIRPS rainfall. Slope = proportional elasticity. Fit to pre-2026 months only (n = 114). R² values are low, indicating rainfall is a weak predictor of network-averaged monthly anomalies.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step9-predict-mar26

# Predict March 2026 with 95% prediction intervals (back-transform from log scale)
newdata_mar26 <- tibble(log_rain = log(373.4))

predict_loglog <- function(model, newdata, label) {
  pred <- predict(model, newdata = newdata, interval = "prediction", level = 0.95)
  tibble(
    nutrient   = label,
    fit        = exp(pred[, "fit"]),
    lo95       = exp(pred[, "lwr"]),
    hi95       = exp(pred[, "upr"]),
    r2         = summary(model)$r.squared,
    slope_p    = summary(model)$coefficients["log_rain", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  )
}

preds <- bind_rows(
  predict_loglog(m_N,  newdata_mar26, "NO3NO2"),
  predict_loglog(m_P,  newdata_mar26, "PO4"),
  predict_loglog(m_Si, newdata_mar26, "SiO2"),
  predict_loglog(m_NH, newdata_mar26, "NH3")
)

# Observed March 2026 network-median fold changes
obs_mar26 <- hui_chirps |>
  filter(year == 2026, month == 3) |>
  select(fc_NO3NO2_med, fc_PO4_med, fc_SiO2_med, fc_NH3_med) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "obs") |>
  mutate(nutrient = str_remove(nutrient, "^fc_") |> str_remove("_med$"))

# Percentile of March 2026 in pre-2026 distribution (raw, without rainfall adjustment)
pre26 <- hui_chirps |> filter(year < 2026)
mar26_row <- hui_chirps |> filter(year == 2026, month == 3)

pct_rank <- function(hist, obs) round(mean(hist < obs, na.rm = TRUE), 3)

percs <- tibble(
  nutrient = c("NO3NO2", "PO4", "SiO2", "NH3"),
  pct_rank = c(
    pct_rank(pre26$fc_NO3NO2_med, mar26_row$fc_NO3NO2_med),
    pct_rank(pre26$fc_PO4_med,    mar26_row$fc_PO4_med),
    pct_rank(pre26$fc_SiO2_med,   mar26_row$fc_SiO2_med),
    pct_rank(pre26$fc_NH3_med,    mar26_row$fc_NH3_med)
  )
)

preds |>
  left_join(obs_mar26, by = "nutrient") |>
  left_join(percs,     by = "nutrient") |>
  mutate(
    outside_95pi = obs > hi95 | obs < lo95,
    obs_over_fit = round(obs / fit, 2)
  ) |>
  select(nutrient, r2, slope_p, fit, lo95, hi95, obs, outside_95pi, pct_rank) |>
  mutate(across(c(r2, slope_p, fit, lo95, hi95, obs), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Nutrient", "R²", "Slope p", "Predicted", "PI lo", "PI hi",
                  "Observed", "Outside 95% PI", "Pctile (pre-2026)"),
    caption   = "March 2026 observed vs model-predicted fold change, with 95% prediction interval. Pctile = percentile of March 2026 in the unadjusted pre-2026 monthly distribution."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig3-rain-nutrient
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "**Figure 3.** Long-term context for the March 2026 Kona Low. **(A)** Monthly Maui island-mean rainfall (CHIRPS, Jun 2016–Mar 2026); March 2026 (373 mm, orange triangle) was the highest single month in the 10-year record by more than 2×. **(B–D)** Monthly station-median fold change (observed / station historical median) vs monthly rainfall for NO₃+NO₂, PO₄, and SiO₂. Line = log-log regression fit to pre-2026 months (n = 114); shaded band = 95% prediction interval; orange triangle = March 2026. R² and slope p-value from log(fc) ~ log(rain) model. The slope for SiO₂ is not significant (p = 0.87), indicating no historical rainfall–SiO₂ relationship in this fixed-station network."

# ── Build prediction ribbons for plotting ─────────────────────────────────────
rain_seq <- tibble(log_rain = seq(log(10), log(400), length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(chirps_mm = exp(log_rain))

make_ribbon <- function(model, label) {
  p <- predict(model, newdata = rain_seq, interval = "prediction")
  rain_seq |>
    mutate(nutrient_f = label,
           fit   = exp(p[, "fit"]),
           lo95  = exp(p[, "lwr"]),
           hi95  = exp(p[, "upr"]))
}

ribbon_df <- bind_rows(
  make_ribbon(m_N,  "NO[3]+NO[2]"),
  make_ribbon(m_P,  "PO[4]"),
  make_ribbon(m_Si, "SiO[2]")
)

# ── Monthly scatter data, long format ─────────────────────────────────────────
nutrient_lvls3 <- c("NO[3]+NO[2]", "PO[4]", "SiO[2]")

scatter_df <- hui_chirps |>
  filter(!is.na(chirps_mm)) |>
  mutate(is_storm = (year == 2026 & month == 3)) |>
  select(ym, chirps_mm, is_storm,
         `NO[3]+NO[2]` = fc_NO3NO2_med,
         `PO[4]`       = fc_PO4_med,
         `SiO[2]`      = fc_SiO2_med) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(nutrient_lvls3),
               names_to = "nutrient_f", values_to = "fc") |>
  filter(!is.na(fc)) |>
  mutate(nutrient_f = factor(nutrient_f, levels = nutrient_lvls3))

ribbon_df <- ribbon_df |>
  mutate(nutrient_f = factor(nutrient_f, levels = nutrient_lvls3))

# R² and p annotations per panel
annot_df <- tibble(
  nutrient_f = factor(nutrient_lvls3, levels = nutrient_lvls3),
  r2_lab     = c(
    sprintf("R² = %.2f, p = %.3f", summary(m_N)$r.squared,
            summary(m_N)$coefficients["log_rain", "Pr(>|t|)"]),
    sprintf("R² = %.2f, p = %.3f", summary(m_P)$r.squared,
            summary(m_P)$coefficients["log_rain", "Pr(>|t|)"]),
    sprintf("R² = %.2f, p = %.3f (n.s.)", summary(m_Si)$r.squared,
            summary(m_Si)$coefficients["log_rain", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  )
)

# ── Panel A: rainfall time series ─────────────────────────────────────────────
chirps_p <- chirps_monthly |> mutate(ym = as.Date(ym),
                                     is_storm = (year == 2026 & month == 3))

pA <- ggplot(chirps_p, aes(x = ym, y = chirps_mm)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = is_storm), width = 27, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is_storm),
             shape = 17, size = 3, colour = "#D55E00") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray72", "TRUE" = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y",
               expand = expansion(add = 20)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 430), breaks = c(0, 100, 200, 300)) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-03-01"), y = 395,
           label = "373 mm", vjust = 0, size = 2.5,
           colour = "#D55E00", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Rainfall (mm/month)", tag = "A") +
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 9)

# ── Panels B–D: fold change vs rainfall ───────────────────────────────────────
pBD <- ggplot(scatter_df, aes(x = chirps_mm, y = fc)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbon_df,
              aes(x = chirps_mm, ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95),
              inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "gray80", alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_line(data = ribbon_df,
            aes(x = chirps_mm, y = fit),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            colour = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed",
             linewidth = 0.35, colour = "gray55") +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, !is_storm),
             size = 1.5, alpha = 0.55, colour = "gray35") +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is_storm),
             shape = 17, size = 3.5, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_text(data = annot_df,
            aes(label = r2_lab),
            x = -Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = -0.5,
            size = 2.3, colour = "gray30", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient_f, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1,
             labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = c(0, 100, 200, 300, 373),
    labels = c("0", "100", "200", "300", "373")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Monthly rainfall (mm)", y = "Fold change\n(station median / historical baseline)",
       tag = "B") +
```

# Spatial Nutrient Patterns {#sec-spatial-patterns}

## Spatial autocorrelation structure {#sec-morans}

> **Step 10.** Moran's I, spatial correlograms, variograms — per nutrient per island.

```{r}
#| label: step10-spatial-prep

# Project to UTM zone 4N (EPSG:32604) — appropriate for all four Hawaiian islands.
# Use non-BDL observations for spatial analyses; log1p-transform responses.
sp_df <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    log1p_SiO2   = log1p(SiO2),
    log1p_NO3NO2 = log1p(NO3NO2),
    log1p_PO4    = log1p(PO4),
    log1p_NH3    = log1p(NH3)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))

sp_sf <- sp_df |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

# Extract UTM coordinates for gstat variograms
sp_sf <- sp_sf |>
  mutate(
    utm_x = st_coordinates(sp_sf)[, 1],
    utm_y = st_coordinates(sp_sf)[, 2]
  )

cat("Samples for spatial analysis:", nrow(sp_sf),
    "| unique locations:", n_distinct(sp_df$latitude, sp_df$longitude), "\n")
cat("By island:", table(sp_df$island), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step10-morans-i

# Moran's I using k-nearest-neighbour spatial weights.
# k=10 globally; k=8 for Molokaʻi (smaller island, fewer nearby samples).
# Row-standardised weights ("W").

run_morans <- function(sf_sub, var, k = 10) {
  coords <- st_coordinates(sf_sub)
  vals   <- st_drop_geometry(sf_sub)[[var]]
  keep   <- !is.na(vals)
  if (sum(keep) < 20) return(NULL)

  nb  <- spdep::knearneigh(coords[keep, ], k = min(k, sum(keep) - 1)) |>
    spdep::knn2nb()
  lw  <- spdep::nb2listw(nb, style = "W")
  mt  <- spdep::moran.test(vals[keep], lw)

  tibble(
    n       = sum(keep),
    morans_I = mt$estimate["Moran I statistic"],
    expected = mt$estimate["Expectation"],
    p_value  = mt$p.value
  )
}

nutrients_sp <- c(
  "log1p_SiO2", "log1p_NO3NO2", "log1p_PO4", "log1p_NH3"
)
islands_sp <- c("All", "O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i")

morans_results <- expand_grid(island = islands_sp, nutrient = nutrients_sp) |>
  mutate(
    result = map2(island, nutrient, \(isl, nut) {
      sub   <- if (isl == "All") sp_sf else sp_sf |> filter(island == isl)
      k_use <- if (isl == "Moloka'i") 8L else 10L
      suppressWarnings(run_morans(sub, nut, k = k_use))
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(result) |>
  mutate(
    nutrient = case_match(nutrient,
      "log1p_SiO2"   ~ "SiO2",
      "log1p_NO3NO2" ~ "NO3+NO2",
      "log1p_PO4"    ~ "PO4",
      "log1p_NH3"    ~ "NH3"
    ),
    sig = case_when(p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                    p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
                    p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
                    TRUE            ~ "n.s.")
  )

morans_results |>
  select(island, nutrient, n, morans_I, expected, p_value, sig) |>
  mutate(across(c(morans_I, expected, p_value), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Global Moran's I for log1p-transformed nutrient concentrations. k-NN weights (k = 10 global and Oʻahu/Maui; k = 8 Molokaʻi). Significant positive values indicate spatial clustering.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step10-variograms
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**Step 10 — Empirical variograms** for log1p-transformed nutrient concentrations (Oʻahu and Maui; UTM zone 4N, EPSG:32604). Point size scales with the number of pairs per bin. SiO₂ shows the clearest distance-decay structure on both islands, consistent with its highest global Moran's I (0.49). NH₄ shows little spatial structure, particularly on Maui."

compute_vgm_df <- function(sf_sub, var, cutoff_m, width_m) {
  sf_filt <- sf_sub |> filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]))
  if (nrow(sf_filt) < 20) return(NULL)
  coords  <- st_coordinates(sf_filt)
  vals    <- st_drop_geometry(sf_filt)[[var]]
  sp_obj  <- sp::SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords = coords,
                                        data   = data.frame(y = vals))
  emp <- suppressWarnings(
    gstat::variogram(y ~ 1, sp_obj, cutoff = cutoff_m, width = width_m)
  )
  as_tibble(emp) |> mutate(nutrient = var)
}

island_params <- tibble(
  island = c("O'ahu", "Maui"),
  cutoff = c(50000,   40000),
  width  = c(4000,    3000)
)

vgm_plot_df <- island_params |>
  mutate(vgm_data = map2(island, cutoff, \(isl, co) {
    wi  <- island_params$width[island_params$island == isl]
    sub <- sp_sf |> filter(island == isl)
    map_dfr(nutrients_sp, \(nut) compute_vgm_df(sub, nut, co, wi))
  })) |>
  unnest(vgm_data) |>
  mutate(
    nutrient_f = factor(
      case_match(nutrient,
        "log1p_SiO2"   ~ "SiO[2]",
        "log1p_NO3NO2" ~ "NO[3]+NO[2]",
        "log1p_PO4"    ~ "PO[4]",
        "log1p_NH3"    ~ "NH[4]"
      ),
      levels = c("NO[3]+NO[2]", "PO[4]", "NH[4]", "SiO[2]")
    ),
    dist_km = dist / 1000
  )

island_cols <- c("O'ahu" = "#1565C0", "Maui" = "#2E7D32")

ggplot(vgm_plot_df, aes(x = dist_km, y = gamma, colour = island, size = np)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, shape = 16) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient_f, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 4), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = island_cols) +
  labs(x = "Distance (km)", y = "Semivariance", colour = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
```

# Terrestrial Connectivity {#sec-connectivity}

## Master analytical dataset {#sec-master-dataset}

> **Steps 2–5.** Load and join all spatial covariates; build `analysis_master`;
> missingness matrix; predictor correlations; define four predictor groups.

```{r}
#| label: step2-load-remaining-covariates
# Load the five covariate sources not yet joined in §2 (Data Inventory):
#   wave height, population density, soil moisture, livestock, NPDES distance.
# All ahupuaa-level joins use composite key ahupuaa + mokupuni.
# pop_density uses 'island' with ʻokina encoding = mokupuni.
# soilmoist and livestock use straight-apostrophe encoding = island;
#   apostrophe variants normalised before joining.

waveheight <- read_csv(here("data", "sample_waveheight.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
pop_dens   <- read_csv(here("data", "pop_density_ahupuaa.csv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
epa        <- read_csv(here("data", "epa_facilities_hi.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
soilmoist  <- read_csv(here("data", "nasa_power_soilmoist.csv"),   show_col_types = FALSE)
livestock  <- read_csv(here("data", "usda_nass_livestock_hi.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Normalise apostrophe variants for island-level joins
normalize_island <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "['\u2018\u2019\u02bc]", "'")

# 1. Wave height — sample_id join
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  left_join(waveheight |> select(sample_id, hs_at_collection_m, hs_mean_m, hs_max_m),
            by = "sample_id")

# 2. Population density — composite key (pop_dens$island uses ʻokina = mokupuni)
pop_clean <- pop_dens |>
  rename(mokupuni = island) |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, mokupuni) |>
  summarise(pop_density_km2 = mean(pop_density_km2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

chem_master <- chem_master |>
  left_join(pop_clean |> select(ahupuaa, mokupuni, pop_density_km2),
            by = c("ahupuaa", "mokupuni"))

# 3. Soil moisture & 4. Livestock — island-level; normalise apostrophe first
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(island_key = normalize_island(island)) |>
  left_join(soilmoist |> mutate(island = normalize_island(island)) |>
              select(island, mean_gwetroot),
            by = c("island_key" = "island")) |>
  left_join(livestock |> mutate(island = normalize_island(island)),
            by = c("island_key" = "island")) |>
  select(-island_key)

# 5. NPDES distance — spatial computation
npdes_pts <- epa |>
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), between(lat, 18, 23), between(lon, -161, -154)) |>
  distinct(lat, lon) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

samples_sf <- chem_master |>
  select(sample_id, latitude, longitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

nearest_npdes <- st_nearest_feature(samples_sf, npdes_pts)
chem_master <- chem_master |>
  mutate(
    dist_to_nearest_npdes_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(samples_sf, npdes_pts[nearest_npdes, ], by_element = TRUE)
    ),
    log_dist_npdes = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: cesspool-exposure-index
#| cache: true

# The two existing cesspool metrics used together in earlier drafts — the 1 km buffer
# count (n_cess_1km) and distance to the nearest cesspool — are moderately collinear
# (Spearman r ≈ -0.79, VIF ≈ 2.7 for both) once density is dropped in favour of the
# buffer count. Rather than force one metric out or accept the collinearity, combine
# proximity and abundance into a single distance-decay "cesspool exposure index":
#   exposure_i = sum_j exp(-d_ij / bandwidth)
# summed over every cesspool j within a cutoff radius of sample i. A cesspool close by
# contributes more than one far away, and multiple nearby cesspools add up — closer AND
# more numerous both increase exposure, which is the "intensity" combination requested.
# bandwidth = 500 m (matches the finer of the two existing buffer scales); cutoff = 2500 m
# (5 bandwidths; weight ≈ 0.007 there, negligible beyond). Rebuilt from the same combined
# cesspool point layer used elsewhere (data/cesspool_points.rds = HCPT layer 32 +
# data/molokai_osds_layer.geojson (Class I filter, n=417) = DOH OSDS 2010 on Molokaʻi), so it inherits
# the same comparability caveat as the other cesspool metrics.

cess_pts_hcpt    <- readRDS(here("data", "cesspool_points.rds")) |> select(geometry)
cess_pts_molokai <- st_read(here("data", "molokai_osds_layer.geojson"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  filter(class_i >= 1) |>
  select(geometry)
all_cesspools_exp <- bind_rows(cess_pts_hcpt, cess_pts_molokai) |>
  st_transform(32604)

samples_exp_sf <- chem_master |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  distinct(sample_id, latitude, longitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

EXP_BW <- 500      # bandwidth, metres
EXP_CUTOFF <- 2500 # cutoff radius, metres

nb_idx <- st_is_within_distance(samples_exp_sf, all_cesspools_exp, dist = EXP_CUTOFF)
cess_exposure_idx <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(samples_exp_sf)), function(i) {
  nb <- nb_idx[[i]]
  if (length(nb) == 0) return(0)
  d <- as.numeric(st_distance(samples_exp_sf[i, ], all_cesspools_exp[nb, ]))
  sum(exp(-d / EXP_BW))
}, numeric(1))

samples_exp_sf$cess_exposure_idx <- cess_exposure_idx

chem_master <- chem_master |>
  left_join(samples_exp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, cess_exposure_idx),
            by = "sample_id")

cat("Cesspool exposure index computed for", sum(!is.na(chem_master$cess_exposure_idx)),
    "of", nrow(chem_master), "samples (0 by construction on Lānaʻi — no cesspools",
    "within the cutoff radius, not missing data).\n")
chem_master |> group_by(island) |>
  summarise(n = n(), n_missing = sum(is.na(cess_exposure_idx)),
            median = round(median(cess_exposure_idx, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            max = round(max(cess_exposure_idx, na.rm = TRUE), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cesspool exposure index by island (distance-decay weighted cesspool count, 500 m bandwidth).")
```
