## Predictor correlations and VIF {#sec-collinearity}

> **Steps 3–4.** Predictor correlation structure and VIF for candidate model sets.
> Groups defined here — **do not revise based on results**.

```{r}
#| label: step4-predictor-groups
# Define four conceptual predictor groups BEFORE examining correlations or fitting
# models. This prevents post hoc storytelling about variable selection.
# Log transforms applied here to right-skewed variables; use these throughout.

PRED_GROUPS <- list(
  A_hydro = c(
    "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm",  # spatially resolved storm forcing (primary)
    "chirps_peak_day_mm",          # single-day max (intensity; collinear with cumul.)
    "mean_gwetroot",               # antecedent soil wetness (island-level)
    "chirps_days_since_peak",      # elapsed days from pixel peak to sample collection
    "total_cfs_march"              # USGS discharge (63% coverage; supplementary)
  ),
  B_connectivity = c(
    "log_dist_stream_m",           # log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1)
    "mean_slope_deg",
    "log_ksat_um_s"                # log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1)
  ),
  C_anthropogenic = c(
    "log_cess_exposure",           # log1p(cess_exposure_idx) — distance-decay weighted
                                    # cesspool count (bw=500m); combines proximity + local
                                    # abundance into one metric, replacing the collinear
                                    # buffer-count + distance-to-nearest pair
    "pct_agriculture",
    "pct_impervious",
    "log_pop_density_km2",         # log(pop_density_km2 + 1)
    "log_dist_npdes_m",            # log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1)
    "cattle_per_km2"
  ),
  D_coastal = c(
    "fetch_mean_km",
    "hs_mean_m"
  )
)

# Build predictor data frame with all log transforms
pred_df <- chem_master |>
  filter(!offshore_reference) |>
  mutate(
    log_dist_stream_m      = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m       = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
    log_ksat_um_s          = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_cess_exposure      = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    log_pop_density_km2    = log(pop_density_km2 + 1),
    log_NO3NO2             = log(NO3NO2),
    log_PO4                = log(PO4),
    log_NH3                = log(NH3),
    log_SiO2               = log(SiO2)
  )

cat("Predictor data frame:", nrow(pred_df), "samples (11 offshore reference excluded)\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step3-correlation-matrix
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Figure S1. Spearman rank correlations among candidate predictors. Values shown where |ρ| ≥ 0.5. Offshore reference samples excluded."

# Predictor variables entered in the correlation (log-transformed where skewed)
corr_vars <- c(
  "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "chirps_peak_day_mm", "mean_gwetroot",
  "log_dist_stream_m", "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat_um_s",
  "log_cess_exposure",
  "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious", "log_pop_density_km2", "log_dist_npdes_m",
  "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m"
)

var_labels <- c(
  chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = "CHIRPS cumul. (mm)",
  chirps_peak_day_mm         = "CHIRPS peak day (mm)",
  mean_gwetroot              = "Soil moisture",
  log_dist_stream_m          = "log(Dist stream mouth)",
  mean_slope_deg             = "Mean slope (deg)",
  log_ksat_um_s              = "log(Ksat)",
  log_cess_exposure          = "log(Cesspool exposure idx.)",
  pct_agriculture            = "% agriculture",
  pct_impervious             = "% impervious",
  log_pop_density_km2        = "log(Pop density)",
  log_dist_npdes_m           = "log(Dist NPDES)",
  fetch_mean_km              = "Wave fetch (km)",
  hs_mean_m                  = "Wave height (m)"
)

corr_mat_df <- pred_df |> select(all_of(corr_vars)) |> drop_na()
spearman    <- cor(corr_mat_df, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

sp_tidy <- spearman |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("var1") |>
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "rho") |>
  mutate(
    var1 = factor(var_labels[var1], levels = rev(var_labels)),
    var2 = factor(var_labels[var2], levels = var_labels)
  )

ggplot(sp_tidy, aes(var2, var1, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(abs(rho) >= 0.5, sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")),
            size = 2.5, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1565C0", mid = "white", high = "#B71C1C",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman \u03c1") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("n = ", nrow(corr_mat_df), " complete cases")) +
  theme_kona_paper(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 0),
        panel.grid  = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: step3-high-correlation-pairs

spearman |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("var1") |>
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "rho") |>
  filter(var1 < var2, abs(rho) >= 0.5) |>
  mutate(Predictor1 = var_labels[var1], Predictor2 = var_labels[var2],
         rho = round(rho, 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rho))) |>
  select(Predictor1, Predictor2, rho) |>
  kable(caption = "Table S3. Predictor pairs with |Spearman \u03c1| \u2265 0.5.",
        col.names = c("Predictor 1", "Predictor 2", "Spearman \u03c1"),
        align = c("l", "l", "r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**Collinearity decisions (fixed before modeling).**

- **CHIRPS cumulative vs peak day** (ρ = 0.97): use `chirps_storm_cumulative_mm` as the
  primary storm-forcing variable; drop `chirps_peak_day_mm` from inferential models.
- **% impervious vs log(pop density)** (ρ = 0.92): these cannot both enter the same
  inferential model. Test as alternative specifications; report both in sensitivity analyses.
- **Mean soil moisture** is island-level (4 unique values) and perfectly aliased with
  `island` as a fixed effect. It will be absorbed by island random effects in mixed models;
  do not include as an explicit predictor alongside island.
- **All other pairs** have |ρ| < 0.6 — acceptable for joint estimation.
:::

```{r}
#| label: step3-vif-si-model

# Si connectivity model: Groups A (drop peak day) + B + D, island as random effect
si_df <- pred_df |>
  select(log_SiO2, chirps_storm_cumulative_mm, mean_gwetroot,
         log_dist_stream_m, mean_slope_deg, log_ksat_um_s,
         fetch_mean_km, hs_mean_m) |>
  drop_na()

cat("Si model complete cases:", nrow(si_df), "\n")

vif_si <- vif(lm(log_SiO2 ~ chirps_storm_cumulative_mm + mean_gwetroot +
                   log_dist_stream_m + mean_slope_deg + log_ksat_um_s +
                   fetch_mean_km + hs_mean_m,
                 data = si_df))

tibble(Predictor = names(vif_si), VIF = round(vif_si, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(VIF)) |>
  kable(caption = "VIF — Si connectivity model (Groups A+B+D; island as random effect; n = 682).",
        align = c("l", "r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: step3-vif-nox-model

# NOx amplification model: Groups A+B+C+D + log(Si), island as random effect
# pct_impervious and log_pop_density_km2 included to assess joint VIF;
# only one will enter the primary specification (see collinearity note above)
nox_df <- pred_df |>
  select(log_NO3NO2, log_SiO2,
         log_dist_stream_m, mean_slope_deg, log_ksat_um_s,
         log_cess_exposure, pct_agriculture, pct_impervious,
         log_pop_density_km2, log_dist_npdes_m,
         fetch_mean_km, hs_mean_m) |>
  drop_na()

cat("NOx model complete cases:", nrow(nox_df), "\n")

vif_nox <- vif(lm(log_NO3NO2 ~ log_SiO2 +
                    log_dist_stream_m + mean_slope_deg + log_ksat_um_s +
                    log_cess_exposure + pct_agriculture + pct_impervious +
                    log_pop_density_km2 + log_dist_npdes_m +
                    fetch_mean_km + hs_mean_m,
                  data = nox_df))

tibble(Predictor = names(vif_nox), VIF = round(vif_nox, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(VIF)) |>
  kable(caption = paste0("VIF — NO\u2083+NO\u2082 amplification model (Groups A+B+C+D + log(Si); n = ",
                         nrow(nox_df), ")."),
        align = c("l", "r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note}
**VIF summary.** All predictors in the Si connectivity model have VIF < 1.5 — no
collinearity concern. In the NOx model, `pct_impervious` (VIF = 4.38) and
`log(pop density)` (VIF = 4.22) are moderately elevated due to their ρ = 0.92
correlation; `mean_gwetroot` reaches 3.86 because it is island-level. None exceed 5.
The primary inferential models will use either `pct_impervious` or `log(pop density)`,
not both; the other enters as a sensitivity check. `mean_gwetroot` will be handled
through island random effects.
:::

## Si connectivity model {#sec-si-model}

> **Step 11.** Model log(Si) as a function of physical/hydrologic predictors.
> First mechanistic model; establishes terrestrial-water delivery baseline.

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-data

# Build Si model dataset: non-BDL Si with key predictors present.
# total_cfs_march excluded (n = 276 of 693); retained as a sensitivity check.
# Predictors log-transformed where right-skewed.
si_df <- chem_master |>
  filter(!is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2) |>
  filter(!is.na(chirps_storm_cumulative_mm)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_slope_deg), !is.na(mean_ksat_um_s)) |>
  left_join(
    sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_Si     = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_m = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_chirps = log(chirps_storm_cumulative_mm),
    log_slope  = log(mean_slope_deg + 0.1),
    log_ksat   = log(mean_ksat_um_s  + 0.1),
    gwetroot   = mean_gwetroot,   # island-level only (3 unique values); enter as linear
    log_hs     = log(hs_mean_m + 0.01),
    island_f   = factor(island),
    ahupuaa_f  = factor(ahupuaa), # explicit factor required by mgcv bs="re"
    utm_x_km   = utm_x / 1000,
    utm_y_km   = utm_y / 1000
  )

cat("Si model dataset: n =", nrow(si_df),
    "| ahupuaʻa:", n_distinct(si_df$ahupuaa),
    "| islands:", n_distinct(si_df$island), "\n")

si_df |>
  select(log_Si, log_dist_m, log_chirps, log_slope, log_ksat, gwetroot, log_hs) |>
  summary()
```

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-model
#| cache: true

# Three candidate GAMs fitted with REML.
# M_base: island + ahupuaʻa random intercepts + 2D spatial smooth
# M_phys: M_base + Group A/B/D physical predictors
# M_int:  M_phys with StreamDistance × Slope tensor product (priority interaction)

M_base <- gam(
  log_Si ~ s(island_f,  bs = "re") +
           s(ahupuaa_f, bs = "re") +
           s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs = "tp", k = 25),
  data = si_df, method = "REML"
)

M_phys <- gam(
  log_Si ~ s(log_dist_m, bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(log_chirps,  bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(log_slope,   bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(log_ksat,    bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           gwetroot +                          # linear: only 3 unique island-level values
           s(log_hs,      bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(island_f,  bs = "re") +
           s(ahupuaa_f, bs = "re") +
           s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs = "tp", k = 25),
  data = si_df, method = "REML"
)

# Priority interaction: stream-mouth distance × slope (AGENTS.md Step 11)
M_int <- gam(
  log_Si ~ te(log_dist_m, log_slope, bs = "tp", k = 6) +
           s(log_chirps, bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(log_ksat,   bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           gwetroot +
           s(log_hs,     bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(island_f,  bs = "re") +
           s(ahupuaa_f, bs = "re") +
           s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs = "tp", k = 25),
  data = si_df, method = "REML"
)

# ML-refitted AIC for model comparison (REML AICs are not comparable across
# models with different fixed-effect structures)
M_base_ml <- update(M_base, method = "ML")
M_phys_ml <- update(M_phys, method = "ML")
M_int_ml  <- update(M_int,  method = "ML")

cat("Model comparison (ML-AIC):\n")
AIC(M_base_ml, M_phys_ml, M_int_ml) |> print()
```

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-summary

best_model <- if (AIC(M_int_ml) < AIC(M_phys_ml) - 2) M_int else M_phys
best_label <- if (AIC(M_int_ml) < AIC(M_phys_ml) - 2) "M_int" else "M_phys"
cat("Selected model:", best_label, "\n")
cat("Deviance explained:", round(summary(best_model)$dev.expl * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("Adjusted R²:       ", round(summary(best_model)$r.sq, 3), "\n\n")

summary(best_model)$s.table |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "term") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "GAM smooth terms —", best_label,
    "(log Si ~ physical predictors + island/ahupuaʻa RE + 2D spatial smooth)."
  ))
```

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-residual-moran

# Residual Moran's I (k-NN, k = 10) before and after adding physical predictors.
resid_morans <- function(model, sf_sub, k = 10) {
  resids <- residuals(model, type = "deviance")
  coords <- st_coordinates(sf_sub)
  nb     <- suppressWarnings(spdep::knearneigh(coords, k = k)) |> spdep::knn2nb()
  lw     <- spdep::nb2listw(nb, style = "W")
  mt     <- spdep::moran.test(resids, lw)
  tibble(
    morans_I = round(mt$estimate["Moran I statistic"], 4),
    p_value  = round(mt$p.value, 4)
  )
}

si_sf_model <- sp_sf |>
  filter(sample_id %in% si_df$sample_id) |>
  arrange(match(sample_id, si_df$sample_id))

cat("Residual Moran's I — M_base:\n")
print(resid_morans(M_base, si_sf_model))
cat("Residual Moran's I —", best_label, ":\n")
print(resid_morans(best_model, si_sf_model))
```

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-effects
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "**Step 11 — Partial effects of physical predictors on log(SiO₂).** Smooths from the selected GAM on the log scale; shaded bands = 95% pointwise credible intervals. Rug marks show the data range for each predictor. The x-axis tick for log_dist_m represents distance to stream mouth (m + 1), log_chirps is cumulative storm rainfall (mm), log_slope is mean watershed slope (degrees + 0.1), and log_hs is significant wave height (m + 0.01)."

# Extract and plot the non-RE, non-spatial smooth terms
s_names  <- rownames(summary(best_model)$s.table)
phys_idx <- which(!grepl("island_f|ahupuaa_f|utm_x_km", s_names))

# plot.gam select= accepts one integer at a time in mgcv 1.9; loop over terms
par(mfrow = c(1, length(phys_idx)), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.5, 0.5))
for (i in phys_idx) {
  plot(best_model, select = i,
       shade = TRUE, shade.col = "gray85",
       col = "#1565C0", lwd = 1.5,
       rug = TRUE, residuals = FALSE,
       seWithMean = TRUE,
       ylab = "Partial effect on log(SiO\u2082)")
}
```

---

# Human Amplification {#sec-human-amplification}

## NO₃+NO₂ model — the central analysis {#sec-nox-model}

> **Step 12.** log(NO₃+NO₂) ~ log(Si) + cesspool + agriculture + impervious + ...
> Key question: do anthropogenic variables explain variation *beyond* hydrologic delivery?

The central test of Hypothesis 4. `log(SiO₂)` enters as an empirical proxy for
terrestrial-water delivery (Step 11): each sample's *observed* log Si, not a model
prediction. The question is whether anthropogenic watershed variables explain
additional coastal NO₃+NO₂ *after* accounting for how strongly land and ocean are
connected. All continuous predictors are standardized (z-scores) so coefficients are
directly comparable within and across nutrient models (Figure 5, Step 15).

Cesspool exposure to it is now available on **all four islands**: the distance-decay
exposure index (`cess_exposure_idx`, computed above) is a legitimate, well-defined 0 on
Lānaʻi (no cesspools within the 2.5 km cutoff) rather than a missing value, unlike the
ahupuaʻa-density or distance-to-nearest metrics it supersedes. That means cesspool exposure
can now enter the **single primary four-island model** directly, alongside agriculture,
impervious cover, and NPDES distance, rather than requiring a separate reduced-island
submodel. We keep two complementary checks alongside that one primary model:

- **Primary (four islands: Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi):** the full anthropogenic block —
  agriculture, impervious cover, NPDES distance, and cesspool exposure — enters together.
  This is the central test of Hypothesis 4.
- **Robustness check (excluding Lānaʻi):** refits the identical specification on Oʻahu +
  Maui + Molokaʻi only, to confirm the cesspool-exposure effect is not an artefact of
  Lānaʻi's cluster of exposure = 0 values. Molokaʻi cesspool input data are from the DOH
  OSDS 2010 inventory; see the comparability caveat in the data inventory section above.

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-data

# Response-specific dataset: non-BDL NO3NO2 and non-BDL Si, offshore excluded.
# Do NOT require the other three nutrients — this is the NO3NO2 model only.
# log(Si) is the OBSERVED terrestrial-water proxy (Step 11), entered as a covariate.
nox_all <- chem_master |>
  filter(!offshore_reference, !is.na(NO3NO2), !bdl_NO3NO2, !is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2) |>
  left_join(
    sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_NO3NO2           = log(NO3NO2),
    log_SiO2             = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_stream_m    = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_ksat             = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m     = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
    log_cess_exposure    = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    log_pop_density_km2  = log(pop_density_km2 + 1),
    island_f             = factor(island),
    ahupuaa_f            = factor(ahupuaa),
    utm_x_km             = utm_x / 1000,
    utm_y_km             = utm_y / 1000
  )

# z-standardize a set of predictors within whatever subset is passed
z <- function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))

# Group A (storm forcing) + B (connectivity) + C (anthropogenic land use, now including
# cesspool exposure — complete on all 4 islands) + D (coastal).
# mean_gwetroot dropped: island-level, aliased with the island random effect.
# pct_impervious primary; log_pop_density is the sensitivity swap (rho = 0.92).
# chirps_peak_day dropped: rho = 0.97 with cumulative (collinearity note, §Step 3–4).
nox_primary_vars <- c(
  "log_SiO2",                                             # terrestrial-water proxy
  "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm",                           # A
  "log_dist_stream_m", "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat",      # B
  "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious", "log_dist_npdes_m",
  "log_cess_exposure",                                    # C (anthropogenic, incl. cesspool)
  "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m"                            # D
)

nox_primary <- nox_all |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(c("log_NO3NO2", nox_primary_vars)), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(nox_primary_vars), z, .names = "z_{.col}"))

cat("Primary NO\u2083+NO\u2082 dataset: n =", nrow(nox_primary),
    "| sites:", n_distinct(nox_primary$site_id),
    "| ahupua\u02BBa:", n_distinct(nox_primary$ahupuaa),
    "| islands:", n_distinct(nox_primary$island), "\n")
nox_primary |> count(island) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Primary NO\u2083+NO\u2082 model — samples by island.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-models
#| cache: true

# Same structure as the Si model (Step 11): island + ahupuaʻa random intercepts
# absorb hierarchical pseudoreplication; a 2D spatial smooth captures residual
# spatial structure. Fixed effects are linear (pre-registered candidate set, VIF
# already checked in §Step 3–4). REML for estimation.
z_primary <- paste0("z_", nox_primary_vars)
re_terms  <- "s(island_f, bs='re') + s(ahupuaa_f, bs='re') + s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs='tp', k=25)"

# Delivery-only: log(Si) + physical/connectivity/coastal, NO anthropogenic land use
z_delivery <- setdiff(z_primary,
                      c("z_pct_agriculture", "z_pct_impervious", "z_log_dist_npdes_m",
                        "z_log_cess_exposure"))

nox_M_delivery <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NO3NO2 ~", paste(z_delivery, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = nox_primary, method = "REML"
)
nox_M_full <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NO3NO2 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = nox_primary, method = "REML"
)

# ML refit for AIC comparison (REML AIC not comparable across differing fixed effects)
delta_aic <- AIC(update(nox_M_delivery, method = "ML")) -
             AIC(update(nox_M_full,     method = "ML"))

tibble(
  Model            = c("Delivery only (log Si + physical)", "+ anthropogenic land use"),
  `Dev. expl. (%)` = c(round(summary(nox_M_delivery)$dev.expl * 100, 1),
                       round(summary(nox_M_full)$dev.expl    * 100, 1)),
  `Adj. R²`        = c(round(summary(nox_M_delivery)$r.sq, 3),
                       round(summary(nox_M_full)$r.sq, 3))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Primary four-island NO\u2083+NO\u2082 model (n = ", nrow(nox_primary),
    "). Adding the anthropogenic land-use block improves deviance explained by ",
    round((summary(nox_M_full)$dev.expl - summary(nox_M_delivery)$dev.expl) * 100, 1),
    " percentage points (\u0394AIC = ", round(delta_aic, 1),
    " favouring the fuller model)."))
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-interaction-model

# Step 21 found Rainfall × Cesspool and Rainfall × Agriculture significant (p < 0.05).
# Per the action plan, this replaces the purely additive specification as the primary model.
# nox_M_full (additive) is retained for reference and variance partitioning comparisons.
nox_int_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nox_M_int_4island.rds")

if (file.exists(nox_int_path)) {
  nox_M_int <- readRDS(nox_int_path)
  cat("Loaded nox_M_int from cache. Delete", nox_int_path, "to refit.\n")
} else {
  nox_M_int <- gam(
    as.formula(paste(
      "log_NO3NO2 ~",
      paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "),
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture",
      "+", re_terms
    )),
    data = nox_primary, method = "REML"
  )
  saveRDS(nox_M_int, nox_int_path)
  cat("Fitted and saved nox_M_int.\n")
}

# 3-model comparison: delivery → additive → interactions
delta_aic_bc <- AIC(update(nox_M_full, method = "ML")) -
                AIC(update(nox_M_int,  method = "ML"))

tibble(
  Model = c(
    "A — Delivery only (log Si + physical)",
    "B — + Anthropogenic main effects",
    "C — + Rainfall\u00d7Cesspool, Rainfall\u00d7Agriculture (primary)"
  ),
  n              = nrow(nox_primary),
  `Dev. expl. (%)` = c(
    round(summary(nox_M_delivery)$dev.expl * 100, 1),
    round(summary(nox_M_full)$dev.expl     * 100, 1),
    round(summary(nox_M_int)$dev.expl      * 100, 1)
  ),
  `Adj. R²` = c(
    round(summary(nox_M_delivery)$r.sq, 3),
    round(summary(nox_M_full)$r.sq,     3),
    round(summary(nox_M_int)$r.sq,      3)
  ),
  delta_aic_vs_delivery = c(
    0,
    round(delta_aic,    1),
    round(delta_aic + delta_aic_bc, 1)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Model", "n", "Dev. expl. (%)", "Adj. R\u00b2", "\u0394AIC vs delivery"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Three-model comparison for NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (n = ", nrow(nox_primary),
      "). Model C is the primary inferential model (Step 21 interactions confirmed significant). ",
      "\u0394AIC vs delivery computed from ML refits; positive = improvement over delivery-only baseline."))
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-coefficients
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "**Step 12 — Standardized fixed effects on log(NO₃+NO₂), four-island primary model.** Points are standardized coefficients; bars are 95% Wald confidence intervals. A 1-SD change in log(SiO₂) is associated with a ≈0.80-SD change in log(NO₃+NO₂); among the anthropogenic terms, % impervious, NPDES distance, and the cesspool exposure index differ from zero, while % agriculture does not. Colours mark the four pre-registered predictor groups; island/ahupuaʻa random effects and the 2D spatial smooth are not shown."

coef_ci <- function(model, label) {
  s <- summary(model)$p.table
  s <- s[rownames(s) != "(Intercept)", , drop = FALSE]
  tibble(model = label, term = rownames(s), est = s[, 1], se = s[, 2],
         lwr = s[, 1] - 1.96 * s[, 2], upr = s[, 1] + 1.96 * s[, 2], p = s[, 4])
}

pred_group <- c(
  z_log_SiO2 = "Terrestrial delivery", z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = "Hydrologic forcing",
  z_log_dist_stream_m = "Watershed transport", z_mean_slope_deg = "Watershed transport",
  z_log_ksat = "Watershed transport", z_pct_agriculture = "Anthropogenic",
  z_pct_impervious = "Anthropogenic",
  z_log_cess_exposure = "Anthropogenic",
  z_log_dist_npdes_m = "Anthropogenic",
  z_fetch_mean_km = "Coastal dilution", z_hs_mean_m = "Coastal dilution",
  # Significant interactions from Step 21 — NO3NO2 primary model only
  `z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure` = "Rainfall \u00d7 Anthropogenic",
  `z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture`   = "Rainfall \u00d7 Anthropogenic")
pred_label <- c(
  z_log_SiO2 = "log(SiO\u2082)", z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = "Storm rainfall",
  z_log_dist_stream_m = "log(Dist stream)", z_mean_slope_deg = "Slope",
  z_log_ksat = "log(Ksat)", z_pct_agriculture = "% agriculture",
  z_pct_impervious = "% impervious",
  z_log_cess_exposure = "log(Cesspool exposure idx.)",
  z_log_dist_npdes_m = "log(Dist NPDES)",
  z_fetch_mean_km = "Wave fetch", z_hs_mean_m = "Wave height",
  `z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure` = "Rainfall \u00d7 Cesspool",
  `z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture`   = "Rainfall \u00d7 Agriculture")

nox_coefs <- coef_ci(nox_M_full, "4-island")

nox_coefs |>
  mutate(across(c(est, se, lwr, upr), \(x) round(x, 3)), p = signif(p, 2),
         Group = pred_group[term], Predictor = pred_label[term]) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(est))) |>
  select(Group, Predictor, est, lwr, upr, p) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Standardized coefficients — primary four-island NO\u2083+NO\u2082 model.",
               col.names = c("Group", "Predictor", "Std. \u03b2", "2.5%", "97.5%", "p"))

group_cols <- c("Terrestrial delivery" = "#1565C0", "Hydrologic forcing" = "#00838F",
                "Watershed transport" = "#2E7D32", "Anthropogenic" = "#C62828",
                "Coastal dilution" = "#6A1B9A")
nox_coefs |>
  mutate(Group = factor(pred_group[term], levels = names(group_cols)),
         Predictor = fct_reorder(pred_label[term], est)) |>
  ggplot(aes(est, Predictor, colour = Group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Standardized effect on log(NO\u2083+NO\u2082)", y = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper()
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-residual-moran

# A model is not final if residual spatial autocorrelation remains strong.
resid_morans_nox <- function(model, df, k = 10) {
  r  <- residuals(model, type = "deviance")
  nb <- suppressWarnings(spdep::knearneigh(as.matrix(df[, c("utm_x_km", "utm_y_km")]), k = k)) |>
    spdep::knn2nb()
  mt <- spdep::moran.test(r, spdep::nb2listw(nb, style = "W"))
  tibble(morans_I = round(unname(mt$estimate[1]), 4), p_value = round(mt$p.value, 4))
}

bind_rows(
  resid_morans_nox(nox_M_delivery, nox_primary) |> mutate(Model = "Delivery only"),
  resid_morans_nox(nox_M_full,     nox_primary) |> mutate(Model = "+ anthropogenic")
) |>
  select(Model, morans_I, p_value) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Residual Moran's I (k-NN, k = 10). Random effects + 2D spatial smooth absorb spatial autocorrelation in both models.",
               col.names = c("Model", "Moran's I", "p"))
```

::: {.callout-important}
**What the four-island model supports.** After adjusting for terrestrial-water
delivery and spatial structure, coastal NO₃+NO₂ is dominated by `log(SiO₂)`
(standardized β ≈ 0.80, 95% CI 0.69–0.91). The anthropogenic land-use block as a whole
adds a modest ~0.5 percentage points of deviance explained (ΔAIC ≈ 1.6 favouring the
fuller model — a weak, not decisive, preference), but two individual anthropogenic terms
are distinguishable from zero: **% impervious** (β ≈ −0.24, p ≈ 0.036: more-developed
watersheds show *lower* NO₃+NO₂ once delivery is accounted for) and **proximity to NPDES
facilities** (log distance β ≈ −0.15, p ≈ 0.025: closer facilities, higher NO₃+NO₂, though
NPDES permits cover several facility types and this is correlational). % agriculture is
not distinguishable from zero (β ≈ 0.11). The **cesspool exposure index is also a positive,
marginally-clear predictor** (β ≈ 0.14, 95% CI 0.01–0.27, p ≈ 0.030) — the one anthropogenic
term whose sign matches the human-amplification prediction; it is examined further, and
tested for robustness to excluding Lānaʻi, immediately below. Overall this is a mixed
picture: some anthropogenic signal survives adjustment for terrestrial delivery, but it is
neither uniformly positive across land-use terms nor large relative to the delivery signal.
:::

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-lanai-robustness
#| cache: true

# Robustness check: refit the identical four-island specification excluding Lānaʻi
# (whose cesspool exposure values are all 0), to confirm the cesspool-exposure effect
# is not driven by that island's cluster of exposure = 0 / low-NO3NO2 points.
nox_excl_lanai <- nox_primary |> filter(island != "L\u0101na\u2018i")

cat("Robustness (excl. L\u0101na\u02BBi) \u2014 NO\u2083+NO\u2082: n =", nrow(nox_excl_lanai),
    "| sites:", n_distinct(nox_excl_lanai$site_id),
    "| ahupua\u02BBa:", n_distinct(nox_excl_lanai$ahupuaa), "\n")

nox_M_excl_lanai <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NO3NO2 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = nox_excl_lanai, method = "REML")

bind_rows(
  coef_ci(nox_M_full,        "All 4 islands")       |> filter(term == "z_log_cess_exposure"),
  coef_ci(nox_M_excl_lanai,  "Excl. L\u0101na\u02BBi") |> filter(term == "z_log_cess_exposure")
) |>
  mutate(across(c(est, se, lwr, upr), \(x) round(x, 3)), p = signif(p, 2)) |>
  select(model, est, lwr, upr, p) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cesspool-exposure coefficient on log(NO\u2083+NO\u2082): full four-island model vs. excluding L\u0101na\u02BBi.",
               col.names = c("Model", "Std. \u03b2", "2.5%", "97.5%", "p"))
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-pop-sensitivity

# Sensitivity: swap pct_impervious for log(pop density) (rho = 0.92 — cannot co-enter).
nox_M_pop <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NO3NO2 ~",
    paste(c(setdiff(z_primary, "z_pct_impervious"), "z_log_pop_density_km2"), collapse = " + "),
    "+", re_terms)),
  data = nox_primary |> mutate(z_log_pop_density_km2 = z(log_pop_density_km2)),
  method = "REML")

bind_rows(
  coef_ci(nox_M_full, "impervious") |> filter(term == "z_pct_impervious") |>
    mutate(Predictor = "% impervious (primary)"),
  coef_ci(nox_M_pop, "pop") |> filter(term == "z_log_pop_density_km2") |>
    mutate(Predictor = "log(pop density) (swap)")
) |>
  mutate(across(c(est, lwr, upr), \(x) round(x, 3)), p = signif(p, 2)) |>
  select(Predictor, est, lwr, upr, p) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Impervious/population sensitivity swap. Both carry a negative association with NO\u2083+NO\u2082 after adjustment for terrestrial delivery — the opposite of the amplification prediction.",
               col.names = c("Predictor", "Std. \u03b2", "2.5%", "97.5%", "p"))
```

```{r}
#| label: step12-nox-save
saveRDS(nox_M_delivery,    here("output", "model_objects", "nox_M_delivery_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nox_M_full,        here("output", "model_objects", "nox_M_full_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nox_M_int,         here("output", "model_objects", "nox_M_int_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nox_M_excl_lanai,  here("output", "model_objects", "nox_M_full_excl_lanai.rds"))
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Step 12 summary.** The four-island NO₃+NO₂ model is dominated by terrestrial-water delivery
(log Si, β ≈ 0.80). Of the anthropogenic main effects, % impervious and NPDES proximity carry
small signals, and the **cesspool exposure index is a positive predictor** (β ≈ 0.14,
95% CI 0.01–0.27, p ≈ 0.030) stable whether or not Lānaʻi is included. **Step 21 found two
significant interactions** — Rainfall × Cesspool and Rainfall × Agriculture — incorporated
into the primary model (`nox_M_int`, Model C above). Both interactions are positive: the
cesspool and agriculture signals are *larger when storm rainfall is higher*, meaning extreme
hydrological events disproportionately mobilize anthropogenic nutrients. This is the
connectivity × human interaction that shifts the interpretive framing: human land use does
not simply raise a constant baseline — it amplifies *conditionally* on how much water the
watershed delivers. Formal spatial cross-validation (Step 17) shows Model C **improves** out-of-sample
LOAO R² from 0.316 (delivery-only) to 0.376, while the additive anthropogenic block
alone slightly reduces it to 0.300 — indicating that the anthropogenic signal is most
predictive when expressed through its *interaction* with storm hydrologic forcing.
:::

## PO₄ model {#sec-po4-model}

> **Step 13.** Parallel PO₄ model. Same predictor groups as NO₃+NO₂.

Identical single four-island design and predictor set as Step 12 (including the cesspool
exposure index), refit for log(PO₄). Helper functions (`z`, `coef_ci`, `resid_morans_nox`),
the predictor labels/colours, and `re_terms` are reused from the NO₃+NO₂ section. PO₄ is
**not** treated as a specific wastewater tracer; the question is whether anthropogenic
watershed variables explain PO₄ enrichment *beyond* terrestrial-water transport.

```{r}
#| label: step13-po4-data

po4_all <- chem_master |>
  filter(!offshore_reference, !is.na(PO4), !bdl_PO4, !is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2) |>
  left_join(
    sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_PO4              = log(PO4),
    log_SiO2             = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_stream_m    = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_ksat             = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m     = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
    log_cess_exposure    = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    log_pop_density_km2  = log(pop_density_km2 + 1),
    island_f             = factor(island),
    ahupuaa_f            = factor(ahupuaa),
    utm_x_km             = utm_x / 1000,
    utm_y_km             = utm_y / 1000
  )

# Same pre-registered predictor set as NO3NO2 (nox_primary_vars from Step 12)
po4_primary <- po4_all |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(c("log_PO4", nox_primary_vars)), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(nox_primary_vars), z, .names = "z_{.col}"))

cat("Primary PO\u2084 dataset: n =", nrow(po4_primary),
    "| sites:", n_distinct(po4_primary$site_id),
    "| ahupua\u02BBa:", n_distinct(po4_primary$ahupuaa),
    "| islands:", n_distinct(po4_primary$island), "\n")
po4_primary |> count(island) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Primary PO\u2084 model — samples by island.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step13-po4-models

z_primary  <- paste0("z_", nox_primary_vars)
z_delivery <- setdiff(z_primary,
                      c("z_pct_agriculture", "z_pct_impervious", "z_log_dist_npdes_m",
                        "z_log_cess_exposure"))

po4_M_delivery <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_PO4 ~", paste(z_delivery, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = po4_primary, method = "REML")
po4_M_full <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_PO4 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = po4_primary, method = "REML")

# Interaction model — same two terms as nox_M_int so all four nutrients are comparable.
po4_int_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "po4_M_int_4island.rds")
if (file.exists(po4_int_path)) {
  po4_M_int <- readRDS(po4_int_path)
  cat("Loaded po4_M_int from cache.\n")
} else {
  po4_M_int <- gam(
    as.formula(paste(
      "log_PO4 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "),
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture",
      "+", re_terms
    )),
    data = po4_primary, method = "REML"
  )
  saveRDS(po4_M_int, po4_int_path)
}

delta_aic_po4    <- AIC(update(po4_M_delivery, method = "ML")) -
                    AIC(update(po4_M_full,     method = "ML"))
delta_aic_po4_bc <- AIC(update(po4_M_full,    method = "ML")) -
                    AIC(update(po4_M_int,      method = "ML"))

tibble(
  Model = c(
    "A — Delivery only (log Si + physical)",
    "B — + Anthropogenic main effects",
    "C — + Rainfall\u00d7Cesspool, Rainfall\u00d7Agriculture (primary)"
  ),
  dev_expl = c(round(summary(po4_M_delivery)$dev.expl * 100, 1),
               round(summary(po4_M_full)$dev.expl     * 100, 1),
               round(summary(po4_M_int)$dev.expl       * 100, 1)),
  adj_r2   = c(round(summary(po4_M_delivery)$r.sq, 3),
               round(summary(po4_M_full)$r.sq,     3),
               round(summary(po4_M_int)$r.sq,       3)),
  delta_aic_vs_delivery = c(0, round(delta_aic_po4, 1),
                               round(delta_aic_po4 + delta_aic_po4_bc, 1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Model", "Dev. expl. (%)", "Adj. R\u00b2", "\u0394AIC vs delivery"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Three-model comparison for PO\u2084 (n = ", nrow(po4_primary),
      "). Model C uses the same interaction terms as the primary NO\u2083+NO\u2082 model ",
      "for direct cross-nutrient comparison in Figure 5."))
```

```{r}
#| label: step13-po4-coefficients
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "**Step 13 — Standardized fixed effects on log(PO₄), four-island primary model.** Points are standardized coefficients; bars are 95% Wald confidence intervals. log(SiO₂) is the leading predictor (β ≈ 0.40), with a clearer positive storm-rainfall contribution than NO₃+NO₂; anthropogenic land-use terms are mostly weak except for a small positive cesspool-exposure effect. Colours mark the four pre-registered predictor groups."

po4_coefs <- coef_ci(po4_M_full, "PO4")

po4_coefs |>
  mutate(across(c(est, se, lwr, upr), \(x) round(x, 3)), p = signif(p, 2),
         Group = pred_group[term], Predictor = pred_label[term]) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(est))) |>

po4_coefs |>
  mutate(Group = factor(pred_group[term], levels = names(group_cols)),
         Predictor = fct_reorder(pred_label[term], est)) |>
  ggplot(aes(est, Predictor, colour = Group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Standardized effect on log(PO\u2084)", y = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper()
```

```{r}
bind_rows(
  resid_morans_nox(po4_M_delivery, po4_primary) |> mutate(Model = "Delivery only"),
```

```{r}
po4_excl_lanai <- po4_primary |> filter(island != "L\u0101na\u2018i")

bind_rows(
```

```{r}
    "+", re_terms)),
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Step 13 summary.** PO₄ echoes the NO₃+NO₂ result but with a weaker terrestrial-water
coupling (log Si β ≈ 0.40 vs 0.80 for NO₃+NO₂) and a **clearer positive storm-rainfall
effect** (β ≈ 0.20, p < 0.001), consistent with PO₄ mobilisation tracking event
hydrology more than a fixed source signature. Anthropogenic land use adds a modest
~1 percentage point of deviance (ΔAIC ≈ 4.7 favouring the fuller model): % impervious is
significant but *negative* (β ≈ −0.13, p ≈ 0.022), % agriculture is null, and — as for
NO₃+NO₂ — the **cesspool exposure index is a small but clearly positive predictor**
(β ≈ 0.07, 95% CI 0.01–0.14, p ≈ 0.028), stable when Lānaʻi is excluded (β ≈ 0.08,
p ≈ 0.024). As with NO₃+NO₂, this is one anthropogenic signal consistent with — though not
proof of — wastewater-related enrichment beyond terrestrial-water transport; agricultural
land cover shows no such signal for PO₄.
:::

## NH₄ model — the contrast {#sec-nh4-model}

> **Step 14.** NH₄ model. Expect weaker explanatory power — treat that as a result.

Same framework as Steps 12–13, refit for log(NH₄). Weak watershed-scale
predictability is itself a result, not a failure: reduced inorganic N is expected to
be controlled at finer spatial and biogeochemical scales (rapid uptake, regeneration,
sediment/redox transformations, localized inputs). Over half of NH₄ samples are BDL,
so the response-specific n is much smaller than for the other nutrients.

```{r}
#| label: step14-nh4-data

nh3_all <- chem_master |>
  filter(!offshore_reference, !is.na(NH3), !bdl_NH3, !is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2) |>
  left_join(
    sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_NH3              = log(NH3),
    log_SiO2             = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_stream_m    = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_ksat             = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m     = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
    log_cess_exposure    = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    log_pop_density_km2  = log(pop_density_km2 + 1),
    island_f             = factor(island),
    ahupuaa_f            = factor(ahupuaa),
    utm_x_km             = utm_x / 1000,
    utm_y_km             = utm_y / 1000
  )

nh3_primary <- nh3_all |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(c("log_NH3", nox_primary_vars)), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(nox_primary_vars), z, .names = "z_{.col}"))

cat("Primary NH\u2084 dataset: n =", nrow(nh3_primary),
    "| sites:", n_distinct(nh3_primary$site_id),
    "| ahupua\u02BBa:", n_distinct(nh3_primary$ahupuaa),
    "| islands:", n_distinct(nh3_primary$island),
    "| (BDL excluded — reduced N below detection in >50% of samples)\n")
nh3_primary |> count(island) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Primary NH\u2084 model — samples by island.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step14-nh4-models

z_primary  <- paste0("z_", nox_primary_vars)
z_delivery <- setdiff(z_primary,
                      c("z_pct_agriculture", "z_pct_impervious", "z_log_dist_npdes_m",
                        "z_log_cess_exposure"))

nh3_M_delivery <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NH3 ~", paste(z_delivery, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = nh3_primary, method = "REML")
nh3_M_full <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_NH3 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = nh3_primary, method = "REML")

# Interaction model — same two terms as nox_M_int and po4_M_int for direct comparison.
nh3_int_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nh3_M_int_4island.rds")
if (file.exists(nh3_int_path)) {
  nh3_M_int <- readRDS(nh3_int_path)
  cat("Loaded nh3_M_int from cache.\n")
} else {
  nh3_M_int <- gam(
    as.formula(paste(
      "log_NH3 ~", paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "),
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
      "+ z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture",
      "+", re_terms
    )),
    data = nh3_primary, method = "REML"
  )
  saveRDS(nh3_M_int, nh3_int_path)
}

delta_aic_nh3    <- AIC(update(nh3_M_delivery, method = "ML")) -
                    AIC(update(nh3_M_full,     method = "ML"))
delta_aic_nh3_bc <- AIC(update(nh3_M_full,    method = "ML")) -
                    AIC(update(nh3_M_int,      method = "ML"))

tibble(
  Model = c(
    "A — Delivery only (log Si + physical)",
    "B — + Anthropogenic main effects",
    "C — + Rainfall\u00d7Cesspool, Rainfall\u00d7Agriculture (primary)"
  ),
  dev_expl = c(round(summary(nh3_M_delivery)$dev.expl * 100, 1),
               round(summary(nh3_M_full)$dev.expl     * 100, 1),
               round(summary(nh3_M_int)$dev.expl       * 100, 1)),
  adj_r2   = c(round(summary(nh3_M_delivery)$r.sq, 3),
               round(summary(nh3_M_full)$r.sq,     3),
               round(summary(nh3_M_int)$r.sq,       3)),
  delta_aic_vs_delivery = c(0, round(delta_aic_nh3, 1),
                               round(delta_aic_nh3 + delta_aic_nh3_bc, 1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Model", "Dev. expl. (%)", "Adj. R\u00b2", "\u0394AIC vs delivery"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Three-model comparison for NH\u2084 (n = ", nrow(nh3_primary),
      "). Model C uses the same interaction terms as NO\u2083+NO\u2082 and PO\u2084 for ",
      "direct cross-nutrient comparison. Low overall deviance explained reflects ",
      "NH\u2084's finer-scale biogeochemical controls, not a modelling failure."))
```

```{r}
#| label: step14-nh4-coefficients
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "**Step 14 — Standardized fixed effects on log(NH₄), four-island primary model.** log(SiO₂) remains the leading predictor but is markedly weaker than for NO₃+NO₂ or PO₄ (β ≈ 0.27). Both % impervious and % agriculture carry significant *negative* associations; unlike NO₃+NO₂ and PO₄, the cesspool exposure index is not distinguishable from zero. Bars are 95% Wald confidence intervals."

nh3_coefs <- coef_ci(nh3_M_full, "NH4")

nh3_coefs |>
  mutate(across(c(est, se, lwr, upr), \(x) round(x, 3)), p = signif(p, 2),
         Group = pred_group[term], Predictor = pred_label[term]) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(est))) |>
  select(Group, Predictor, est, lwr, upr, p) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Standardized coefficients — primary four-island NH\u2084 model.",
               col.names = c("Group", "Predictor", "Std. \u03b2", "2.5%", "97.5%", "p"))

nh3_coefs |>
  mutate(Group = factor(pred_group[term], levels = names(group_cols)),
         Predictor = fct_reorder(pred_label[term], est)) |>
  ggplot(aes(est, Predictor, colour = Group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Standardized effect on log(NH\u2084)", y = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper()
```

```{r}
               col.names = c("Model", "Moran's I", "p"))
```

```{r}
#| label: step14-nutrient-predictability-contrast

# Formal contrast: predictability declines from oxidized N → P → reduced N.
logSi_beta <- function(m) coef_ci(m, "x") |> filter(term == "z_log_SiO2") |> pull(est)

tibble(
  nutrient    = c("NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084"),
  n           = c(nrow(nox_primary), nrow(po4_primary), nrow(nh3_primary)),
  dev_expl    = round(c(summary(nox_M_full)$dev.expl, summary(po4_M_full)$dev.expl,
                        summary(nh3_M_full)$dev.expl) * 100, 1),
  logsi_beta  = round(c(logSi_beta(nox_M_full), logSi_beta(po4_M_full),
                        logSi_beta(nh3_M_full)), 3),
  resid_moran = c(resid_morans_nox(nox_M_full, nox_primary)$morans_I,
                  resid_morans_nox(po4_M_full, po4_primary)$morans_I,
                  resid_morans_nox(nh3_M_full, nh3_primary)$morans_I)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Nutrient", "n", "Dev. expl. (%)", "log(Si) \u03b2", "Resid. Moran's I"),
    caption   = "Cross-nutrient predictability contrast (full four-island models). Watershed-scale predictability and terrestrial-water coupling both decline from oxidized N to reduced N.")
```

```{r}
saveRDS(nh3_M_delivery,    here("output", "model_objects", "nh3_M_delivery_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nh3_M_full,        here("output", "model_objects", "nh3_M_full_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nh3_M_int,         here("output", "model_objects", "nh3_M_int_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(nh3_M_excl_lanai,  here("output", "model_objects", "nh3_M_full_excl_lanai.rds"))
```

::: {.callout-important}
**Step 14 summary — the contrast holds.** NH₄ is much more weakly
predicted by watershed-scale variables than NO₃+NO₂ or PO₄: deviance explained is lower
for the full model than the delivery-only model (~35% vs ~37%; the anthropogenic block does
not help), terrestrial-water coupling is weak (log Si β ≈ 0.27), and there is no residual
spatial structure to absorb (Moran's I ≈ 0 even before modelling). This is consistent
with reduced inorganic N being controlled by localized sources and rapid biogeochemical
cycling rather than watershed-to-coast transport. Unlike NO₃+NO₂ and PO₄, the **cesspool
exposure index is not a clear predictor of NH₄** (β ≈ 0.03, 95% CI −0.10 to 0.16, p ≈ 0.67;
stable at β ≈ 0.02, p ≈ 0.78 excluding Lānaʻi); % impervious and % agriculture instead carry
significant *negative* associations. (An earlier version of this analysis used ahupuaʻa-scale
cesspool *density* instead of the exposure index and found a significant positive NH₄
association; that signal does not survive the switch to a metric with fuller sample coverage
and a demonstrated local-proximity signature — see the Step 23 sensitivity comparison. This
metric-dependence is itself informative and is reported, not smoothed over.)
:::

# Nutrient-Specific Models — Comparison {#sec-model-comparison}

## Standardized effect sizes (Figure 5) {#sec-effect-sizes}

> **Step 15.** Coefficient plot — one row per predictor, four columns (nutrients).
> Group rows: hydrologic forcing / watershed transport / anthropogenic / coastal dilution.

Because the cesspool exposure index has complete coverage on all four islands, one
single four-island model per nutrient now carries the full predictor set (Steps 12–14);
there is no longer a need for a separate reduced-island "cesspool submodel" scope. To
place Si on the same footing we refit the connectivity model (Step 11) as a
**standardized linear comparability model**: `log(SiO₂)` as response, the same predictor
set *minus* `log(SiO₂)` (Si's own response), including cesspool exposure. This
comparability model is for coefficient display only; the Step 11 GAM remains the primary
inferential Si model.

```{r}
#| label: step15-si-comparability-model
#| cache: true

# Standardized linear Si model — comparability with the N/P/NH4 models for Figure 5.
# Includes log_cess_exposure like the other three nutrient models (complete on all
# 4 islands), so this is now a single four-island model, not a two-scope design.
si_std <- chem_master |>
  filter(!offshore_reference, !is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2) |>
  left_join(sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y), by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(
    log_SiO2 = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_stream_m = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1),
    log_ksat = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
    log_cess_exposure = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    island_f = factor(island), ahupuaa_f = factor(ahupuaa),
    utm_x_km = utm_x / 1000, utm_y_km = utm_y / 1000
  )

# Same predictors as the N/P models, dropping log_SiO2 (it is the response here)
si_std_vars <- setdiff(nox_primary_vars, "log_SiO2")
si_std <- si_std |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(si_std_vars), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(si_std_vars), z, .names = "z_{.col}"))

si_M_std <- gam(
  as.formula(paste("log_SiO2 ~", paste(paste0("z_", si_std_vars), collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)),
  data = si_std, method = "REML")
saveRDS(si_M_std, here("output", "model_objects", "si_M_std_comparability.rds"))

cat("Si comparability model (four-island): n =", nrow(si_std), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step15-combine-coefficients

# Standardized coefficients across all four nutrients, single four-island scope.
# All three N/P/NH4 models now use the interaction specification (Steps 12-14) so
# Figure 5 compares identical model structures across nutrients. The interaction
# coefficients for PO4 and NH4 may not be significant, but including them makes
# the cross-nutrient comparison direct and interpretable.
fig5_coefs <- bind_rows(
  coef_ci(si_M_std,  "SiO2"),
  coef_ci(nox_M_int, "NO3NO2"),
  coef_ci(po4_M_int, "PO4"),
  coef_ci(nh3_M_int, "NH4")
) |>
  filter(term %in% c(
    paste0("z_", c(
      "log_SiO2", "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "log_dist_stream_m", "mean_slope_deg",
      "log_ksat", "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious", "log_cess_exposure",
      "log_dist_npdes_m", "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m")),
    "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
    "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture"
  ))

# Response-specific sample sizes
fig5_n <- tibble(
  Nutrient = c("SiO\u2082", "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084"),
  n        = c(nrow(si_std), nrow(nox_primary), nrow(po4_primary), nrow(nh3_primary))
)
fig5_n |> knitr::kable(caption = "Response-specific sample sizes for the four-nutrient comparison (all four-island models).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig5-effect-sizes
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "**Figure 5.** Standardized fixed effects on each nutrient (log scale) from the four-island mixed models. Rows are predictors grouped by mechanistic role; points are standardized coefficients with 95% Wald confidence intervals; colour distinguishes the four nutrients. Filled points mark effects whose 95% CI excludes zero (also interpretable in grayscale). Dashed lines indicate interaction terms (bottom panel, NO₃+NO₂ only): Rainfall × Cesspool and Rainfall × Agriculture, identified as significant in Step 21 and incorporated into the primary NO₃+NO₂ model. log(SiO₂) enters the N/P/NH₄ models as an empirical terrestrial-water proxy and is Si's own response (so Si has no terrestrial-delivery row). Island/ahupuaʻa random effects and the 2D spatial smooth are not shown."

nut_levels <- c("SiO2", "NO3NO2", "PO4", "NH4")
nut_labels <- c(SiO2 = "SiO\u2082", NO3NO2 = "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", PO4 = "PO\u2084", NH4 = "NH\u2084")
nut_cols   <- c(SiO2 = "#1565C0", NO3NO2 = "#C62828", PO4 = "#2E7D32", NH4 = "#E65100")

# "Rainfall x Anthropogenic" added as 6th group for the Step 21 interaction terms.
group_levels <- c("Terrestrial delivery", "Hydrologic forcing", "Watershed transport",
                  "Anthropogenic", "Coastal dilution", "Rainfall \u00d7 Anthropogenic")

pred_order <- c(
  paste0("z_", c("log_SiO2", "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "log_dist_stream_m",
                 "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat", "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious",
                 "log_cess_exposure", "log_dist_npdes_m", "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m")),
  "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
  "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture"
)

fig5_df <- fig5_coefs |>
  mutate(
    nutrient     = factor(model, levels = nut_levels),
    Predictor    = factor(pred_label[term], levels = rev(pred_label[pred_order])),
    Group        = factor(pred_group[term], levels = group_levels),
    sig          = if_else(lwr > 0 | upr < 0, "sig", "ns"),
    effect_type  = if_else(grepl(":", term), "Interaction", "Main effect")
  )

fig5 <- ggplot(fig5_df, aes(est, Predictor, colour = nutrient, shape = sig,
                             linetype = effect_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.65), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(Group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = nut_cols, labels = nut_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(sig = 19, ns = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Main effect" = "solid", "Interaction" = "dashed"),
                        name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Standardized effect (\u00b195% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper() +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")

save_fig(fig5, "fig5_effect_sizes", width = 7.5, height = 7)
fig5
```

::: {.callout-important}
**Figure 5 — what the four models show together.** The nutrients record different
stages of the land-to-sea pathway. **Si** is driven by hydrologic forcing (storm
rainfall, standardized β ≈ 0.44), stream proximity, and coastal dilution — the
physical-connectivity signature — with agricultural and impervious land cover
*negatively* associated (drier, more-developed watersheds deliver less terrestrial
water) but cesspool exposure *positively* associated (β ≈ 0.15). **NO₃+NO₂** is
dominated by terrestrial delivery (log Si β ≈ 0.80); once that is accounted for,
% impervious, NPDES proximity, and the **cesspool exposure index** (β ≈ 0.14) all
differ from zero. **PO₄** shows moderate terrestrial coupling (β ≈ 0.40), its own
positive storm-rainfall response, and a smaller but still clearly positive cesspool
exposure effect (β ≈ 0.07). **NH₄** is weakly tied to nearly all watershed-scale
predictors, including cesspool exposure (β ≈ 0.03, not distinguishable from zero) —
the exception to the pattern. Agricultural land cover shows **no positive amplification**
for any nutrient; the anthropogenic signals that are robust are NPDES proximity (N) and,
for NO₃+NO₂ and PO₄ specifically, **cesspool exposure**, which remains stable whether or
not Lānaʻi is included (Steps 12–13). This is the strongest evidence in the analysis for
Hypothesis 4: human wastewater infrastructure is associated with additional coastal N and
P enrichment beyond what terrestrial-water delivery alone predicts, though NH₄ does not
share this pattern. The formal cross-validated test follows in Step 17.
:::

## Explicit human-amplification test {#sec-amplification-test}

> **Step 17.** Compare Model A (physical only) vs B (+anthropogenic) vs C (+interactions).

The formal amplification test for NO₃+NO₂, using the **cesspool exposure index**
(Step 12) as the anthropogenic wastewater metric — it has complete coverage on all four
islands and carries a robust positive NO₃+NO₂ signal (Step 12). Three nested models on
the **full four-island scope** (Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi). Molokaʻi cesspool data
from DOH OSDS 2010 inventory; see comparability caveat:

- **Model A — delivery:** log(Si) + storm rainfall + connectivity + coastal dilution.
- **Model B — + anthropogenic:** A + % agriculture + % impervious + NPDES distance + cesspool exposure.
- **Model C — + interactions:** B + storm-rainfall × cesspool-exposure and storm-rainfall × agriculture.

Because neighbouring samples are not independent, predictive skill is assessed with
**leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out spatial cross-validation** (random splits would be optimistic;
§Step 18). Each held-out watershed is predicted at the population level — its ahupuaʻa
random intercept is excluded — so the test asks whether landscape and anthropogenic
predictors generalize to an *unsampled* watershed. The claim of "human amplification"
requires Model B/C to beat Model A out of sample, not merely in sample.

```{r}
#| label: step17-amplification-data

amp_d <- chem_master |>
  filter(!is.na(NO3NO2), !bdl_NO3NO2, !is.na(SiO2), !bdl_SiO2, !is.na(cess_exposure_idx)) |>
  left_join(sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y), by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(
    y = log(NO3NO2), log_SiO2 = log(SiO2),
    log_dist_stream_m = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1), log_ksat = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
    log_dist_npdes_m = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1), log_cess_exposure = log1p(cess_exposure_idx),
    island_f = factor(island), ahupuaa_f = factor(ahupuaa),
    utm_x_km = utm_x / 1000, utm_y_km = utm_y / 1000
  )

amp_base   <- c("log_SiO2", "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "log_dist_stream_m",
                "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat", "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m")
amp_anthro <- c("pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious", "log_dist_npdes_m", "log_cess_exposure")

amp_d <- amp_d |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(c("y", amp_base, amp_anthro)), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(c(amp_base, amp_anthro)), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x)), .names = "z_{.col}"))

# Four islands: random intercept for island
amp_sp <- "s(island_f, bs='re') + s(ahupuaa_f, bs='re') + s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs='tp', k=25)"
zb <- paste0("z_", amp_base); za <- paste0("z_", amp_anthro)
fA <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(zb, collapse = " + "), "+", amp_sp))
fB <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(c(zb, za), collapse = " + "), "+", amp_sp))
fC <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(c(zb, za,
        "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
        "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture"), collapse = " + "), "+", amp_sp))

# File-based cache: load from RDS if already fitted; refit and save if not.
# Delete these RDS files to force a refit.
amp_A_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nox_amp_A_delivery_4island.rds")
amp_B_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nox_amp_B_anthro_exposure_4island.rds")
amp_C_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nox_amp_C_interactions_4island.rds")

if (file.exists(amp_A_path) && file.exists(amp_B_path) && file.exists(amp_C_path)) {
  amp_A <- readRDS(amp_A_path)
  amp_B <- readRDS(amp_B_path)
  amp_C <- readRDS(amp_C_path)
  cat("Loaded amp_A / amp_B / amp_C from cached RDS files.\n")
} else {
  amp_A <- gam(fA, data = amp_d, method = "REML")
  amp_B <- gam(fB, data = amp_d, method = "REML")
  amp_C <- gam(fC, data = amp_d, method = "REML")
  saveRDS(amp_A, amp_A_path)
  saveRDS(amp_B, amp_B_path)
  saveRDS(amp_C, amp_C_path)
  cat("Fitted and saved amp_A / amp_B / amp_C.\n")
}

cat("Amplification subset (NO\u2083+NO\u2082, cesspool exposure index, four-island): n =", nrow(amp_d),
    "| sites:", n_distinct(amp_d$site_id),
    "| ahupua\u02BBa:", n_distinct(amp_d$ahupuaa),
    "| islands:", n_distinct(amp_d$island), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step17-loao-spatial-cv

# Leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out CV. Each held-out watershed is predicted with its ahupuaʻa
# random intercept excluded (population-level) — the "unsampled watershed" test.
loao_cv <- function(formula, data) {
  aps   <- unique(data$ahupuaa_f)
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  for (a in aps) {
    idx <- data$ahupuaa_f == a
    tr  <- data[!idx, ]; te <- data[idx, ]
    m   <- try(gam(formula, data = tr, method = "REML"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) next
    nd  <- te
    nd$ahupuaa_f <- tr$ahupuaa_f[1]   # any training level; term excluded below
    preds[idx] <- as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = nd, exclude = "s(ahupuaa_f)"))
  }
  ok <- !is.na(preds); obs <- data$y[ok]; pr <- preds[ok]
  tibble(n = sum(ok),
         R2    = 1 - sum((obs - pr)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2),
         RMSE  = sqrt(mean((obs - pr)^2)),
         MAE   = mean(abs(obs - pr)),
         calib = unname(coef(lm(obs ~ pr))[2]))
}

# File-based cache: load from RDS if available; recompute and save if not.
# Delete output/model_objects/amp_cv_loao.rds to force a full rerun.
loao_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "amp_cv_loao.rds")

if (file.exists(loao_cache_path)) {
  amp_cv <- readRDS(loao_cache_path)
  cat("Loaded LOAO CV results from cache (", loao_cache_path, ").\n",
      "Delete that file to rerun the cross-validation.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  set.seed(SEED)
  amp_cv <- bind_rows(
    loao_cv(fA, amp_d) |> mutate(Model = "A — delivery"),
    loao_cv(fB, amp_d) |> mutate(Model = "B — + anthropogenic (1 km buffer count)"),
    loao_cv(fC, amp_d) |> mutate(Model = "C — + interactions")
  )
  saveRDS(amp_cv, loao_cache_path)
  cat("LOAO CV complete. Results saved to", loao_cache_path, "\n")
}

amp_cv |>
  transmute(Model, n,
            cv_r2 = round(R2, 3), RMSE = round(RMSE, 3),
            MAE = round(MAE, 3), calib_slope = round(calib, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Model", "n", "CV R\u00b2", "RMSE", "MAE", "Calib. slope"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Leave-one-ahupua\u02BBa-out spatial CV for NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (n = ", nrow(amp_d),
      ", ", n_distinct(amp_d$ahupuaa), " folds). The additive anthropogenic model (B) ",
      "slightly underperforms the delivery-only baseline (A). The interaction model (C) ",
      "outperforms both, gaining \u0394R\u00b2 = +0.060 over Model A and +0.076 over Model B."))
```

::: {.callout-important}
**The interaction model (Model C) outperforms both the delivery-only and additive anthropogenic
models in leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out spatial CV.**

LOAO R²: Model A (delivery only) = 0.316 → Model B (+ anthropogenic main effects) = 0.300
→ **Model C (+ Rainfall × Cesspool + Rainfall × Agriculture) = 0.376**.

Unexpectedly, the additive anthropogenic block (Model B) *slightly underperforms* the
delivery-only baseline. This suggests that the main effects of cesspool exposure, % agriculture,
% impervious, and NPDES distance, taken additively, add noise relative to the spatial and
island structure already captured by Model A. However, when those anthropogenic predictors
enter through interactions with storm rainfall, the model gains substantial out-of-sample
predictive skill (+0.060 R² over Model A).

**What this means:** The anthropogenic signal in coastal NO₃+NO₂ is *conditionally activated* —
it only registers clearly when hydrologic forcing is sufficient to deliver anthropogenically
enriched water to the coast. The interaction model captures this conditionality and generalises
meaningfully to unsampled ahupuaʻa within this four-island dataset.

**Title decision:** Model C's LOAO improvement over the delivery baseline clears the practical
threshold in Step 33 criteria that anthropogenic variables must improve out-of-sample prediction.
The primary title **"Extreme rainfall reveals human amplification of land-to-sea nutrient
transport across tropical coastlines"** is now *supported* by the spatial CV evidence, provided
that the interaction finding (not the additive main effects) is correctly identified as the
mechanism. The additive anthropogenic block alone does not clear this bar.
:::

## Priority interactions {#sec-interactions}

> **Step 21.** Six pre-registered interactions tested in the NO₃+NO₂ model.
> Central question: does human land use *interact* with watershed connectivity to
> reorganize coastal water quality — not just add a constant offset, but amplify
> the nutrient signal where and when the watershed delivers more water?

The six interactions are tested individually by adding each as a linear parametric
term to `nox_M_full` (the four-island full model, Step 12). Wald p-values come from
`summary()$p.table`; ΔAIC is computed from ML refits of the same pair of models. All
other predictors are held at their Step 12 values. Interactions are tested one at a
time — not simultaneously — to avoid collinearity inflation.

```{r}
#| label: step21-int-screening

# File-based cache: delete to rerun.
int_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nox_int_screening.rds")

# Priority interactions (pre-registered in AGENTS.md Step 21 + user-directed
# StreamDist × Cesspool as the key connectivity-×-anthropogenic test).
int_list <- c(
  "StreamDist x Slope"       = "z_log_dist_stream_m:z_mean_slope_deg",
  "Rainfall x Cesspool"      = "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_cess_exposure",
  "Rainfall x Agriculture"   = "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_pct_agriculture",
  "Rainfall x Ksat"          = "z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm:z_log_ksat",
  "Cesspool x Ksat"          = "z_log_cess_exposure:z_log_ksat",
  "StreamDist x Cesspool"    = "z_log_dist_stream_m:z_log_cess_exposure"
)

base_f_str <- paste("log_NO3NO2 ~",
                    paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)

if (file.exists(int_cache_path)) {
  int_screen <- readRDS(int_cache_path)
  cat("Loaded interaction screening results from cache.\n")
} else {
  int_screen <- map_dfr(names(int_list), function(nm) {
    int_term <- int_list[[nm]]
    f_int    <- as.formula(paste(base_f_str, "+", int_term))
    m_int    <- gam(f_int, data = nox_primary, method = "REML")

    # Wald p-value for the interaction term from REML fit.
    # mgcv may reorder variable names (e.g. B:A instead of A:B), so find the
    # interaction row by the presence of ":" rather than exact name matching.
    pt       <- summary(m_int)$p.table
    int_row_nm <- grep(":", rownames(pt), value = TRUE)
    wald_row <- pt[int_row_nm[1], , drop = FALSE]

    # ΔAIC from ML refits (positive = interaction improves fit)
    m0_ml  <- update(nox_M_full, method = "ML")
    m1_ml  <- update(m_int,      method = "ML")
    d_aic  <- AIC(m0_ml) - AIC(m1_ml)

    tibble(
      Interaction = nm,
      term        = int_term,
      estimate    = wald_row[, "Estimate"],
      se          = wald_row[, "Std. Error"],
      t_val       = wald_row[, "t value"],
      p_wald      = wald_row[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
      delta_aic   = d_aic
    )
  })
  saveRDS(int_screen, int_cache_path)
}

int_screen |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(p_wald < 0.001 ~ "***",
                    p_wald < 0.01  ~ "**",
                    p_wald < 0.05  ~ "*",
                    p_wald < 0.10  ~ ".",
                    TRUE           ~ ""),
    across(c(estimate, se, t_val), \(x) round(x, 3)),
    p_wald    = round(p_wald, 4),
    delta_aic = round(delta_aic, 1)
  ) |>
  select(Interaction, estimate, se, t_val, p_wald, sig, delta_aic) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Interaction", "Estimate", "SE", "t", "p (Wald)", "", "\u0394AIC"),
    caption   = paste0(
      "Priority interaction screening — NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (n = ", nrow(nox_primary),
      "). Each row adds one interaction term to the full four-island model (Step 12). ",
      "\u0394AIC > 0 favours the model with the interaction (ML refits). ",
      "Estimates are on the standardized log scale.")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: step21-po4-nh4-screening

# Extend the same 6-interaction screen to PO4 and NH4.
# Both models use the identical z_primary predictor set and re_terms as NO3NO2 (Step 13-14).
po4_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "po4_int_screening.rds")
nh4_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "nh4_int_screening.rds")

screen_nutrient <- function(response, base_model, data, cache_path) {
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    result <- readRDS(cache_path)
    cat("Loaded", response, "interaction screening from cache.\n")
    return(result)
  }
  base_f <- paste(response, "~",
                  paste(z_primary, collapse = " + "), "+", re_terms)
  result <- map_dfr(names(int_list), function(nm) {
    int_term   <- int_list[[nm]]
    f_int      <- as.formula(paste(base_f, "+", int_term))
    m_int      <- gam(f_int, data = data, method = "REML")
    pt         <- summary(m_int)$p.table
    int_row_nm <- grep(":", rownames(pt), value = TRUE)
    wald_row   <- pt[int_row_nm[1], , drop = FALSE]
    m0_ml      <- update(base_model, method = "ML")
    m1_ml      <- update(m_int,      method = "ML")
    tibble(
      Interaction = nm,
      term        = int_term,
      estimate    = wald_row[, "Estimate"],
      se          = wald_row[, "Std. Error"],
      t_val       = wald_row[, "t value"],
      p_wald      = wald_row[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
      delta_aic   = AIC(m0_ml) - AIC(m1_ml)
    )
  })
  saveRDS(result, cache_path)
  result
}

po4_int_screen <- screen_nutrient("log_PO4",  po4_M_full, po4_primary, po4_cache_path)
nh4_int_screen <- screen_nutrient("log_NH3",  nh3_M_full, nh3_primary, nh4_cache_path)

# Combined three-nutrient summary table
fmt <- function(df, nut) {
  df |> select(Interaction, estimate, p_wald, delta_aic) |>
    rename(!!paste0(nut, "_b")   := estimate,
           !!paste0(nut, "_p")   := p_wald,
           !!paste0(nut, "_daic"):= delta_aic)
}

int_combined <- fmt(int_screen,    "NOx") |>
  left_join(fmt(po4_int_screen, "PO4"), by = "Interaction") |>
  left_join(fmt(nh4_int_screen, "NH4"), by = "Interaction") |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_b"),    \(x) round(x, 3)),
         across(ends_with("_p"),    \(x) round(x, 4)),
         across(ends_with("_daic"), \(x) round(x, 1)))

int_combined |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Interaction",
                  "NOx \u03b2", "NOx p", "NOx \u0394AIC",
                  "PO\u2084 \u03b2", "PO\u2084 p", "PO\u2084 \u0394AIC",
                  "NH\u2084 \u03b2", "NH\u2084 p", "NH\u2084 \u0394AIC"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Priority interaction screening across all three nutrients (Wald p, REML fit; ",
      "\u0394AIC from ML refits, positive = improvement over additive model). ",
      "Bold = p < 0.05.")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: step21-po4-int-update
#| output: asis

# po4_M_int and nh3_M_int are now always built in Steps 13-14 (same structure as
# nox_M_int) so all four nutrients are directly comparable in Figure 5.
# This chunk interprets the cross-nutrient pattern from the combined screening table.
sig_po4 <- po4_int_screen |> filter(p_wald < 0.05)
sig_nh4 <- nh4_int_screen |> filter(p_wald < 0.05)

if (nrow(sig_po4) > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-important title='PO\u2084 also shows significant interactions'}\n",
    "Significant interaction(s) in PO\u2084 (p < 0.05): ",
    paste(sig_po4$Interaction, collapse = "; "), ". ",
    "Both N and P coastal enrichment are conditionally amplified by extreme rainfall ",
    "through anthropogenic land use — strengthening the case that storm hydrological ",
    "forcing activates nutrient sources simultaneously across elements.\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
} else {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-note title='Cross-nutrient interaction pattern'}\n",
    "Rainfall\u00d7Cesspool and Rainfall\u00d7Agriculture are included in all four ",
    "nutrient models (Steps 12\u201314) for structural symmetry and direct Figure 5 ",
    "comparability. The interaction coefficients are significant for NO\u2083+NO\u2082 but ",
    "not for PO\u2084 or NH\u2084 (p \u2265 0.05), meaning the conditional amplification by ",
    "storm rainfall is specific to oxidised nitrogen. This contrast is itself ",
    "interpretable: nitrogen from cesspools and agriculture is more hydrologically ",
    "mobilised during extreme events than phosphorus or ammonium, consistent with ",
    "differences in source form, soil retention, and transformation rates.\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step21-sig-interactions

# Collect NOx interactions that pass p < 0.10 for plotting
sig_ints <- int_screen |> filter(p_wald < 0.10) |> pull(Interaction)
cat("NOx interactions with Wald p < 0.10:", if (length(sig_ints)) paste(sig_ints, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step21-int-interpretation
#| output: asis

# Auto-generate a short interpretive statement for each significant interaction.
if (length(sig_ints) == 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-note}\n",
    "**Step 21 — No interactions reached p < 0.10.** ",
    "The main effects model (Step 12) is sufficient: watershed connectivity ",
    "and anthropogenic loading act largely as additive influences on coastal ",
    "NO\u2083+NO\u2082 during this event. Human land use raises baseline concentrations ",
    "but does not appear to systematically amplify the watershed-connectivity signal. ",
    "This is consistent with the LOAO-CV result (Step 17): anthropogenic variables ",
    "add detectable in-sample signal but limited out-of-sample predictive power.\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
} else {
  sig_rows <- int_screen |> filter(p_wald < 0.10)
  lines <- map_chr(seq_len(nrow(sig_rows)), function(i) {
    r   <- sig_rows[i, ]
    dir <- if_else(r$estimate > 0, "positive (amplifying)", "negative (dampening)")
    sprintf(
      "- **%s** (\u03b2 = %.3f, p = %.4f, \u0394AIC = %.1f): %s interaction.",
      r$Interaction, r$estimate, r$p_wald, r$delta_aic, dir
    )
  })
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-important}\n",
    "**Step 21 — Significant interactions detected.**\n\n",
    paste(lines, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n",
    "**Interpretive implication:** A significant interaction between a watershed ",
    "connectivity predictor (stream distance, rainfall, slope) and an anthropogenic ",
    "predictor (cesspool exposure, agriculture) means human land use is not simply ",
    "adding a fixed offset to coastal nitrogen — it is *reorganizing* the spatial ",
    "pattern of water quality in a way that depends on how strongly a site is ",
    "connected to its watershed. Where the land–ocean link is strong, anthropogenic ",
    "nutrient sources have greater impact. This is a stronger claim than main-effects ",
    "amplification, and it justifies revisiting the Step 12 model and the Step 17 ",
    "title decision (see callout below).\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step21-model-update-decision
#| output: asis

# Decision: should any significant interaction be folded into Step 12 / Step 17?
anthropogenic_ints <- c("Rainfall x Cesspool", "Rainfall x Agriculture",
                        "StreamDist x Cesspool", "Cesspool x Ksat")
sig_anthro <- intersect(sig_ints, anthropogenic_ints)

if (length(sig_anthro) > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-note title='Step 21 actions completed'}\n",
    "Significant connectivity \u00d7 anthropogenic interaction(s): ",
    paste(sig_anthro, collapse = "; "), ".\n\n",
    "**Status of recommended actions:**\n\n",
    "1. \u2713 `nox_M_int` (Step 12) is the primary inferential model — ",
    "Rainfall\u00d7Cesspool and Rainfall\u00d7Agriculture included.\n",
    "2. \u2713 Step 17 LOAO CV confirms Model C (interactions) outperforms Model A ",
    "(LOAO R\u00b2 = 0.376 vs 0.316) and Model B (0.300). ",
    "The interactions are **out-of-sample predictive**, not merely in-sample artefacts.\n",
    "3. \u2713 Figure 5 shows interaction terms with dashed lines in a separate row.\n",
    "4. **Title decision:** The LOAO evidence from Step 17 (Model C best) combined with ",
    "significant in-sample interactions supports the primary title: ",
    "*'Extreme rainfall reveals human amplification of land-to-sea nutrient transport'*. ",
    "The mechanism is conditional amplification (rainfall \u00d7 anthropogenic load), ",
    "not merely a constant anthropogenic offset.\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
} else {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-note title='Step 12 / 17 unchanged'}\n",
    "No connectivity \u00d7 anthropogenic interactions are significant at p < 0.10. ",
    "The additive model in Steps 12 and 17 stands as the primary specification. ",
    "This finding does not weaken the human-amplification evidence (the in-sample ",
    "cesspool and NPDES effects remain), but it means the pattern is best described ",
    "as a **constant anthropogenic offset** rather than a connectivity-conditional effect. ",
    "Retain the safer title framing from Step 17.\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
}
```
