```{r}
#| label: fig6-interaction-effects
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**Figure 6 — Conditional amplification of coastal NO₃+NO₂ by anthropogenic land use during extreme rainfall.** Marginal-effect predictions from the primary NO₃+NO₂ model (nox_M_int; Step 12), showing how the relationship between cumulative storm rainfall and predicted log(NO₃+NO₂) changes with **(A)** cesspool exposure index and **(B)** % agricultural land cover. Lines show population-level predictions (island, ahupuaʻa, and spatial random effects excluded) holding all other predictors at their means. The three lines per panel correspond to the Q10 (low; blue dashed), Q50 (median; grey solid), and Q90 (high; red dashed) of the respective moderator. The positive interaction slopes confirm that extreme rainfall amplifies coastal nitrogen enrichment *more strongly* where anthropogenic sources are denser. Leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out CV (Step 17) confirms that this pattern generalises to unsampled watersheds (Model C LOAO R² = 0.376 vs 0.316 for delivery-only). **Note on Panel B:** the y-axis is capped at 78 µmol L⁻¹ (99th percentile of observed NO₃+NO₂). At the extreme combination of Q90 agriculture (35%) and maximum storm rainfall the model predicts above this range — a region of sparse predictor space where out-of-sample reliability is low. The divergence direction is ecologically meaningful; the absolute magnitude at the extreme should not be taken literally. Tick-mark spacing reflects the underlying log scale of the model."

# Standardisation parameters for axis back-transformation
chirps_mu <- mean(nox_primary$chirps_storm_cumulative_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
chirps_sd <- sd(nox_primary$chirps_storm_cumulative_mm,  na.rm = TRUE)
cess_mu   <- mean(nox_primary$log_cess_exposure, na.rm = TRUE)
cess_sd   <- sd(nox_primary$log_cess_exposure,   na.rm = TRUE)
ag_mu     <- mean(nox_primary$pct_agriculture,   na.rm = TRUE)
ag_sd     <- sd(nox_primary$pct_agriculture,     na.rm = TRUE)

z_vars_nox <- paste0("z_", nox_primary_vars)
excl_re_f6 <- c("s(island_f)", "s(ahupuaa_f)", "s(utm_x_km,utm_y_km)")

# Helper: marginal predictions from nox_M_int varying one z-predictor,
# stratifying the moderator at Q10 / Q50 / Q90.
marginal_int <- function(x_z, mod_z, n = 80, mod_q_probs = c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90)) {
  x_seq  <- seq(quantile(nox_primary[[x_z]],  0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(nox_primary[[x_z]],  0.98, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = n)
  mod_qs <- quantile(nox_primary[[mod_z]], mod_q_probs, na.rm = TRUE)
  lvls   <- c("Low (Q10)", "Median (Q50)", "High (Q90)")
  map_dfr(seq_along(mod_qs), function(qi) {
    nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(0, n, length(z_vars_nox),
                               dimnames = list(NULL, z_vars_nox)))
    nd[[x_z]]    <- x_seq
    nd[[mod_z]]  <- mod_qs[[qi]]
    nd$island_f  <- nox_primary$island_f[1]
    nd$ahupuaa_f <- nox_primary$ahupuaa_f[1]
    nd$utm_x_km  <- mean(nox_primary$utm_x_km, na.rm = TRUE)
    nd$utm_y_km  <- mean(nox_primary$utm_y_km, na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(
      rain_mm   = x_seq * chirps_sd + chirps_mu,
      pred      = as.numeric(predict(nox_M_int, newdata = nd, exclude = excl_re_f6,
                                     newdata.guaranteed = TRUE)),
      Moderator = factor(lvls[[qi]], levels = lvls)
    )
  })
}

int_col <- c("Low (Q10)"    = "#1565C0",
             "Median (Q50)" = "#757575",
             "High (Q90)"   = "#C62828")
int_lty <- c("Low (Q10)" = "dashed", "Median (Q50)" = "solid", "High (Q90)" = "dashed")

# ── Panel A: Rainfall × Cesspool ─────────────────────────────────────────────
cess_dat  <- marginal_int("z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "z_log_cess_exposure")
cess_q_z  <- quantile(nox_primary$z_log_cess_exposure, c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90), na.rm = TRUE)
cess_q_raw <- expm1(cess_q_z * cess_sd + cess_mu)  # back from log1p(cess_exposure_idx)
cess_leg  <- sprintf(c("Low (Q10; idx = %.1f)", "Median (Q50; idx = %.1f)",
                        "High (Q90; idx = %.1f)"), cess_q_raw)

# Direct line labels via ggrepel (cleaner than a legend for 2-panel figure)
# 99th percentile of observed log-NOx: cap for both panels so Panel B's
# extreme-combination extrapolation does not distort the shared y scale.
y_obs_99 <- quantile(nox_primary$log_NO3NO2, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)  # ≈ 4.36

make_f6_panel <- function(dat, rug_x_col, y_lab, tag_lbl, line_labels,
                           y_max = y_obs_99) {
  lab_dat <- dat |>
    group_by(Moderator) |>
    slice_max(rain_mm, n = 1) |>
    mutate(label = line_labels[as.integer(Moderator)])
  ggplot(dat, aes(rain_mm, pred, colour = Moderator, linetype = Moderator)) +
    geom_rug(data = nox_primary, aes(x = nox_primary[[rug_x_col]], y = NULL),
             sides = "b", alpha = 0.20, linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0, show.legend = FALSE) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = lab_dat, aes(label = label, colour = Moderator),
      direction = "y", nudge_x = 30, hjust = 0, size = 2.5,
      show.legend = FALSE, segment.size = 0.3, segment.alpha = 0.4,
      max.overlaps = 20
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = int_col) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = int_lty) +
    # Back-transform y-axis ticks: data are log(µmol/L), display as µmol/L
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = log(c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 75)),
      labels = c("0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "25", "75")
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(NA, y_max), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Cumulative storm rainfall (mm)", y = y_lab, tag = tag_lbl) +
    theme_kona_paper() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 80, 6, 8))
}

pA <- make_f6_panel(
  cess_dat, "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm",
  "Predicted NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (\u03bcmol L\u207b\u00b9)", "A",
  c("Low (Q10)\nidx = 0", "Median (Q50)\nidx = 2.0", "High (Q90)\nidx = 45")
)

# ── Panel B: Rainfall × Agriculture ──────────────────────────────────────────
ag_dat   <- marginal_int("z_chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "z_pct_agriculture")
ag_q_z   <- quantile(nox_primary$z_pct_agriculture, c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90), na.rm = TRUE)
ag_q_raw <- ag_q_z * ag_sd + ag_mu   # proportions (0–1); ×100 for percentage display

pB <- make_f6_panel(
  ag_dat, "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", NULL, "B",
  sprintf(c("Low (Q10)\n%.0f%% ag.", "Median (Q50)\n%.1f%% ag.", "High (Q90)\n%.0f%% ag."),
          ag_q_raw * 100)
)

fig6 <- pA | pB
fig6
save_fig(fig6, "fig6_interactions", width = 8, height = 4.5)
```

# Variance Partitioning {#sec-variance-partitioning}

> **Step 16 (Figure S3 — Supplementary).** Unique and shared explanatory power for each driver group
> across all four nutrients. The interaction marginal-effects figure is now Figure 6 in the main text.

For each nutrient we quantify the unique contribution of the pre-registered driver
groups (Step 4) by fitting a nested sequence of GAMs that adds one block at a time, in
a fixed order decided *before* looking at results:

$$M_0 \to M_1 (+\text{Hydrology}) \to M_2 (+\text{Connectivity}) \to M_3 (+\text{Human}) \to M_4 (+\text{Coastal})$$

Every model in the sequence — including $M_0$ — retains the same island + ahupuaʻa
random intercepts and 2D spatial smooth (`re_terms`, Steps 11–12), so an increase in
deviance explained from $M_{k-1}$ to $M_k$ is attributable only to the fixed-effect
block added at step $k$, not to spatial structure. $M_0$'s own deviance explained is
reported as a fifth "Spatial/Island" share, addressing driver group (5) from Step 16's
instructions (spatial/island structure) even though it is not one of the four columns
in the original Figure 6 sketch. `log(SiO₂)` — the empirical terrestrial-water-delivery
proxy used in the N/P/NH₄ models (Steps 12–14) — is folded into the **Connectivity**
block for those three nutrients: it is the observed integrator of stream-mouth
distance, slope, and Ksat for a given sample, so grouping it with the raw physical
connectivity terms avoids inventing a fifth ad hoc category. For the Si model itself,
Connectivity uses only the raw physical terms (Si cannot be its own predictor).

This uses the **four-island primary scope** (Tier 1, Steps 11–13; agriculture +
impervious + NPDES distance as the Human block) so that all four nutrients — including
Si — are partitioned on a consistent, maximal-coverage sample. Cesspool-specific
human-amplification is the more targeted question posed by Step 17's three-island
test (Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi) and is not repeated here. As with all deviance-explained
decompositions, shares are **descriptive, not causal**, and are sensitive to the fixed
entry order when blocks share variance (e.g. storm rainfall and stream distance are
both physically upstream of Si); they should be read as "unique association given this
pre-registered order," not as proof that a block is mechanistically necessary.

```{r}
#| label: step16-variance-partition-models
#| cache: true

# Driver-group blocks (pre-registered in Step 4; fixed order set before fitting).
grp_hydrology    <- c("chirps_storm_cumulative_mm")                              # A
grp_connect_phys <- c("log_dist_stream_m", "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat")         # B
grp_anthro       <- c("pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious", "log_dist_npdes_m")   # C (no cesspool; 4-island scope)
grp_coastal      <- c("fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m")                             # D

# Fit the nested M0->M4 sequence for one response/dataset. `connect_vars` lets the
# Si model use only the raw physical connectivity terms, while N/P/NH4 models fold
# in log(SiO2) as the empirical connectivity/delivery proxy (see prose above).
fit_nested_vp <- function(response, data, connect_vars) {
  zv <- function(v) paste0("z_", v)
  build_f <- function(vars) as.formula(paste(
    response, "~",
    if (length(vars) > 0) paste(paste(zv(vars), collapse = " + "), "+") else "",
    re_terms))

  list(
    M0 = gam(build_f(character(0)),                                              data = data, method = "REML"),
    M1 = gam(build_f(grp_hydrology),                                             data = data, method = "REML"),
    M2 = gam(build_f(c(grp_hydrology, connect_vars)),                            data = data, method = "REML"),
    M3 = gam(build_f(c(grp_hydrology, connect_vars, grp_anthro)),                data = data, method = "REML"),
    M4 = gam(build_f(c(grp_hydrology, connect_vars, grp_anthro, grp_coastal)),   data = data, method = "REML")
  )
}

vp_devexpl <- function(models) vapply(models, function(m) summary(m)$dev.expl, numeric(1))

# Increments in deviance explained = each block's unique share given the fixed order.
vp_shares <- function(models, nutrient, data) {
  de <- vp_devexpl(models)
  tibble(
    nutrient        = nutrient,
    spatial_island  = de[["M0"]],
    hydrology       = de[["M1"]] - de[["M0"]],
    connectivity    = de[["M2"]] - de[["M1"]],
    human           = de[["M3"]] - de[["M2"]],
    coastal         = de[["M4"]] - de[["M3"]],
    residual        = 1 - de[["M4"]],
    n               = nrow(data),
    n_sites         = n_distinct(data$site_id),
    n_ahupuaa       = n_distinct(data$ahupuaa),
    n_islands       = n_distinct(data$island)
  )
}

vp_models_si  <- fit_nested_vp("log_SiO2",   si_std,       grp_connect_phys)
vp_models_nox <- fit_nested_vp("log_NO3NO2", nox_primary,  c(grp_connect_phys, "log_SiO2"))
vp_models_po4 <- fit_nested_vp("log_PO4",    po4_primary,  c(grp_connect_phys, "log_SiO2"))
vp_models_nh3 <- fit_nested_vp("log_NH3",    nh3_primary,  c(grp_connect_phys, "log_SiO2"))

vp_table <- bind_rows(
  vp_shares(vp_models_si,  "SiO\u2082",         si_std),
  vp_shares(vp_models_nox, "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", nox_primary),
  vp_shares(vp_models_po4, "PO\u2084",          po4_primary),
  vp_shares(vp_models_nh3, "NH\u2084",          nh3_primary)
)

# Save every final (M4) model, plus the full nested list, for reproducibility.
saveRDS(vp_models_si,  here("output", "model_objects", "vp_models_Si_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(vp_models_nox, here("output", "model_objects", "vp_models_NOx_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(vp_models_po4, here("output", "model_objects", "vp_models_PO4_4island.rds"))
saveRDS(vp_models_nh3, here("output", "model_objects", "vp_models_NH4_4island.rds"))
```

```{r}
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste0(
      "Variance partitioning (% deviance explained) among five driver-group blocks, ",
      "four-island primary scope. Blocks entered in the pre-registered order Hydrology ",
      "\u2192 Connectivity \u2192 Human \u2192 Coastal (log(SiO\u2082) folded into Connectivity ",
      "for the N/P/NH\u2084 models); shares are increments in GAM deviance explained and are ",

    col.names = c("Nutrient", "Spatial/Island", "Hydrology", "Connectivity", "Human",
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "**Figure S3 (Supplementary).** Variance partitioning among five mechanistic driver-group blocks (four-island primary scope), shown as % deviance explained from the nested M0\u2192M4 GAM sequence (Step 16). Blocks are entered in the pre-registered order Hydrology \u2192 Connectivity \u2192 Human \u2192 Coastal; log(SiO\u2082) is folded into Connectivity for NO\u2083+NO\u2082, PO\u2084, and NH\u2084 as the empirical terrestrial-delivery proxy. Shares are descriptive increments, not independent/causal contributions, and are sensitive to the fixed entry order when blocks share variance. ::: {.callout-warning}
```
**Why the Spatial/Island block dominates, and why that does not mean the other blocks
are unimportant.** Across all four nutrients, $M_0$ (island + ahupuaʻa random
intercepts + 2D spatial smooth, no fixed effects) alone explains 30–48% of deviance —
far more than any single driver-group block added afterward. This is expected, not a
modelling failure: most physical and anthropogenic predictors here (`mean_slope_deg`,
`mean_ksat_um_s`, `pct_agriculture`, `pct_impervious`, cesspool metrics) are **ahupuaʻa-
level constants** — every sample from the same ahupuaʻa has the identical value — so
once the ahupuaʻa random intercept is in the model, these variables are largely
*aliased* with ahupuaʻa identity and can add only a small residual, within-group-type
signal on top of it. Their standardized coefficients in Figure 5 (fit *without* the
ahupuaʻa-level ceiling that a random intercept imposes) remain the primary evidence for
their effects; Figure 6 should be read as "how much *additional, ahupuaʻa-independent*
variance a block explains," not as an estimate of each mechanism's total importance.
Consistent with this, **Connectivity's comparatively large share for NO₃+NO₂ and PO₄
(≈17–18%, vs. <1% for Si's own physical-only Connectivity block) is driven almost
entirely by `log(SiO₂)`** — the one connectivity-block term that varies at the *sample*
level rather than the ahupuaʻa level, and therefore is not absorbed by the random
intercept. This reinforces, via an independent route, Step 12's core finding that
terrestrial-water delivery (measured by Si) is the dominant explainable signal for
oxidized N and P once spatial structure is accounted for.
:::

# Out-of-Sample Hotspot Prediction {#sec-hotspot-prediction}

## Spatial cross-validation {#sec-spatial-cv}

> **Step 18.** Blocked spatial CV and leave-one-island-out CV.
> Report R², RMSE, MAE, calibration slope.

### Part A — Spatial block CV (leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out) {#sec-step18a-loao}

Ahupuaʻa are contiguous traditional watershed polygons and serve as natural spatial blocks
for cross-validation. Holding out all samples from one ahupuaʻa at a time — then predicting
those samples using only the fixed-effect landscape predictors (the ahupuaʻa random intercept
is excluded from predictions) — tests whether the model generalizes to **unsampled
watersheds**. This is a more stringent test than random sample splitting because nearby
samples within the same ahupuaʻa are predicted together, preventing spatial autocorrelation
from inflating apparent skill.

Step 17 ran LOAO for the three nested amplification models on the NO₃+NO₂ subset. Here
the test is extended to all four primary nutrient models on their full respective datasets.

### Part B — Leave-one-island-out CV {#sec-step18b-loio}

The most demanding generalizability test: train on three islands, predict the fourth. Both
the island and ahupuaʻa random intercepts are excluded from predictions; the 2D spatial
smooth is also excluded (it would extrapolate across open ocean to island locations not seen
in training). Only the fixed-effect landscape predictors are used. This asks whether
physical and anthropogenic landscape relationships are consistent enough across islands to
permit cross-island prediction.

```{r}
#| label: step18-cv-helpers

# ── Step 18 — CV helper functions ───────────────────────────────────────────

# Compute standard CV performance metrics
cv_metrics <- function(obs, pred) {
  ok   <- !is.na(obs) & !is.na(pred)
  obs  <- obs[ok]; pred <- pred[ok]
  calib <- tryCatch(unname(coef(lm(obs ~ pred))[2]), error = \(e) NA_real_)
  tibble(
    n           = length(obs),
    CV_R2       = round(1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2), 3),
    CV_RMSE     = round(sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2)), 3),
    CV_MAE      = round(mean(abs(obs - pred)), 3),
    calib_slope = round(calib, 3)
  )
}

# Leave-one-ahupuaʻa-out spatial CV.
# The ahupuaʻa RE is excluded during prediction (population-level = unsampled watershed).
# The island RE and spatial smooth are retained (within-island extrapolation).
loao_cv_gam <- function(model, data, response_col) {
  form  <- formula(model)
  aps   <- unique(data$ahupuaa_f)
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  n_skip <- 0L
  for (a in aps) {
    idx <- data$ahupuaa_f == a
    tr  <- data[!idx, ]; te <- data[idx, ]
    if (nrow(tr) < 30) { n_skip <- n_skip + 1L; next }
    m <- try(gam(form, data = tr, method = "REML"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) { n_skip <- n_skip + 1L; next }
    nd <- te
    # Assign a training-level factor so predict does not fail on unseen level
    nd$ahupuaa_f <- factor(tr$ahupuaa_f[1], levels = levels(tr$ahupuaa_f))
    preds[idx] <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = nd, exclude = "s(ahupuaa_f)"))
    )
  }
  if (n_skip > 0) message("LOAO: ", n_skip, " folds skipped (n_train < 30 or fit error)")
  obs <- data[[response_col]]
  cv_metrics(obs, preds) |>
    mutate(n_folds = length(aps), n_skipped = n_skip, .before = n)
}

# Leave-one-island-out CV.
# Excludes island RE, ahupuaʻa RE, AND the 2D spatial smooth — only fixed-effect
# landscape predictors are used, since the spatial smooth cannot extrapolate
# meaningfully across the open ocean to a new island's coordinate space.
loio_cv_gam <- function(model, data, response_col) {
  form    <- formula(model)
  islands <- unique(as.character(data$island))
  preds   <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  isl_tag <- character(nrow(data))

  # Identify the 2D spatial smooth term name (usually "s(utm_x_km,utm_y_km)")
  smooth_names <- sapply(model$smooth, \(s) s$label)
  sp_smooth    <- grep("utm_x_km", smooth_names, value = TRUE)

  exclude_terms <- c("s(island_f)", "s(ahupuaa_f)", sp_smooth)

  for (isl in islands) {
    idx <- data$island == isl
    tr  <- data[!idx, ]; te <- data[idx, ]
    if (nrow(tr) < 30) next
    m <- try(gam(form, data = tr, method = "REML"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) next

    nd <- te
    # Assign training-level factors (excluded terms, so values don't matter)
    nd$island_f  <- factor(tr$island_f[1],  levels = levels(tr$island_f))
    nd$ahupuaa_f <- factor(tr$ahupuaa_f[1], levels = levels(tr$ahupuaa_f))

    # Find spatial smooth name on the NEW model (same structure, different levels)
    new_sp <- grep("utm_x_km", sapply(m$smooth, \(s) s$label), value = TRUE)

    preds[idx] <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = nd,
                         exclude = c("s(island_f)", "s(ahupuaa_f)", new_sp)))
    )
    isl_tag[idx] <- isl
  }

  obs <- data[[response_col]]
  list(
    overall    = cv_metrics(obs, preds) |>
                   mutate(n_islands = length(islands), .before = n),
    per_island = tibble(island = isl_tag, obs = obs, pred = preds) |>
                   filter(!is.na(pred)) |>
                   group_by(island) |>
                   summarise(cv_metrics(obs, pred), .groups = "drop"),
    obs        = obs[!is.na(preds)],
    pred       = preds[!is.na(preds)],
    island     = isl_tag[!is.na(preds)]
  )
}

cat("Step 18 CV helper functions defined: cv_metrics, loao_cv_gam, loio_cv_gam\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step18-loao-cv
#| cache: false

# Run LOAO-CV for all four primary nutrient models.
# File-based cache: delete the RDS to force a full rerun.
loao_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "step18_loao_cv_all4.rds")

if (file.exists(loao_cache_path)) {
  step18_loao <- readRDS(loao_cache_path)
  cat("Loaded LOAO CV results from cache.\nDelete", loao_cache_path, "to rerun.\n")
} else {
  set.seed(SEED)
  cat("Running LOAO-CV for all four primary models (this may take ~10 min)...\n")

  # Si — primary model (whichever was selected in Step 11: M_phys or M_int)
  cat("  Si:", best_label, "...\n")
  si_loao  <- loao_cv_gam(best_model, si_df,      "log_Si")

  # NO3+NO2 — primary interaction model (nox_M_int; includes Rainfall×Cesspool +
  #            Rainfall×Agriculture, identified as significant in Step 21 and
  #            confirmed as out-of-sample predictive in Step 17 LOAO).
  cat("  NO3+NO2 (interaction model) ...\n")
  nox_loao <- loao_cv_gam(nox_M_int, nox_primary, "log_NO3NO2")

  # PO4 — full four-island model
  cat("  PO4 ...\n")
  po4_loao <- loao_cv_gam(po4_M_full, po4_primary, "log_PO4")

  # NH4 — full four-island model
  cat("  NH4 ...\n")
  nh3_loao <- loao_cv_gam(nh3_M_full, nh3_primary, "log_NH3")

  step18_loao <- list(Si = si_loao, NOx = nox_loao, PO4 = po4_loao, NH4 = nh3_loao)
  saveRDS(step18_loao, loao_cache_path)
  cat("LOAO CV complete. Results saved to", loao_cache_path, "\n")
}

bind_rows(step18_loao, .id = "Nutrient") |>
  mutate(across(c(CV_R2, CV_RMSE, CV_MAE, calib_slope), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Nutrient", "Folds", "Skipped", "n",
                  "CV R\u00b2", "RMSE", "MAE", "Calib. slope"),
    caption = paste0(
      "Step 18A \u2014 Leave-one-ahupua\u02BBa-out spatial CV for all four primary nutrient",
      " models (REML GAMs, population-level prediction). Each fold holds out one",
      " ahupua\u02BBa\u2019s samples and predicts them from the landscape fixed effects",
      " only (ahupua\u02BBa RE excluded). NO\u2083+NO\u2082 uses the primary interaction",
      " model (nox_M_int, Step 12/21); Si, PO\u2084, NH\u2084 use their additive primary models.",
      " RMSE and MAE are on the log scale."
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: step18-loio-cv
#| cache: false

# Run LOIO-CV for all four primary nutrient models.
loio_cache_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "step18_loio_cv_all4.rds")

if (file.exists(loio_cache_path)) {
  step18_loio <- readRDS(loio_cache_path)

} else {
  set.seed(SEED)
  cat("Running LOIO-CV for all four primary models (4 folds each)...\n")

  si_loio  <- loio_cv_gam(best_model, si_df,      "log_Si")
  nox_loio <- loio_cv_gam(nox_M_int, nox_primary, "log_NO3NO2")
  po4_loio <- loio_cv_gam(po4_M_full, po4_primary, "log_PO4")
  nh3_loio <- loio_cv_gam(nh3_M_full, nh3_primary, "log_NH3")

  step18_loio <- list(Si = si_loio, NOx = nox_loio, PO4 = po4_loio, NH4 = nh3_loio)
  saveRDS(step18_loio, loio_cache_path)
  cat("LOIO CV complete. Results saved to", loio_cache_path, "\n")
}

# ── Overall LOIO summary table ───────────────────────────────────────────────
bind_rows(lapply(step18_loio, \(x) x$overall), .id = "Nutrient") |>
  mutate(across(c(CV_R2, CV_RMSE, CV_MAE, calib_slope), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(

    )
  )
```

## Random forest — applied prediction {#sec-random-forest}

> **Step 19.** Continuous-response RF for all four nutrients.
> Use for hotspot identification, not inference.

Random forests are fitted here as a **prediction** tool, not an inferential one. The
question is: *can publicly available landscape data identify coastal nutrient hotspots
after an extreme event?* Because RF makes no assumptions about linearity or random
effect structure, and because `island` enters as an ordinary categorical predictor
(rather than a random intercept), RF has more flexibility than the GAMs in Steps 11–14
and should improve LOAO predictive performance. Variable importance is reported for
*exploration*, not as causal attribution — correlated predictors share importance and
the ranking is sensitive to collinearity.

RF predictor sets mirror the corresponding GAM: the Si model uses physical connectivity
predictors; NO₃+NO₂, PO₄, and NH₄ use the same standardised predictor set as
Steps 12–14 (raw log-transformed values, not z-scaled) plus `island` as a categorical
predictor.

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-setup

# ── Predictor sets ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Mirror the GAM predictor names (log-transformed, but NOT z-scaled).
# island is added as a categorical predictor for all four RF models.

si_rf_vars  <- c("log_dist_m", "log_chirps", "log_slope", "log_ksat",
                  "gwetroot", "log_hs", "island")

nox_rf_vars <- c("log_SiO2", "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "log_dist_stream_m",
                  "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat", "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious",
                  "log_dist_npdes_m", "log_cess_exposure", "fetch_mean_km",
                  "hs_mean_m", "island")

# Display groups and labels for importance plots (parallel to pred_group / pred_label)
rf_group <- c(
  log_SiO2                   = "Terrestrial delivery",
  chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = "Hydrologic forcing",
  log_dist_stream_m          = "Watershed transport",
  mean_slope_deg             = "Watershed transport",
  log_ksat                   = "Watershed transport",
  pct_agriculture            = "Anthropogenic",
  pct_impervious             = "Anthropogenic",
  log_dist_npdes_m           = "Anthropogenic",
  log_cess_exposure          = "Anthropogenic",
  fetch_mean_km              = "Coastal dilution",
  hs_mean_m                  = "Coastal dilution",
  log_dist_m                 = "Watershed transport",
  log_chirps                 = "Hydrologic forcing",
  log_slope                  = "Watershed transport",
  log_ksat                   = "Watershed transport",
  log_hs                     = "Coastal dilution",
  gwetroot                   = "Hydrologic forcing",
  island                     = "Island"
)

rf_label <- c(
  log_SiO2                   = "log(SiO\u2082)",
  chirps_storm_cumulative_mm = "Storm rainfall",
  log_dist_stream_m          = "log(Dist. stream)",
  mean_slope_deg             = "Slope",
  log_ksat                   = "log(Ksat)",
  pct_agriculture            = "% agriculture",
  pct_impervious             = "% impervious",
  log_dist_npdes_m           = "log(Dist. NPDES)",
  log_cess_exposure          = "log(Cesspool exposure)",
  fetch_mean_km              = "Wave fetch",
  hs_mean_m                  = "Wave height",
  log_dist_m                 = "log(Dist. stream)",
  log_chirps                 = "log(Storm rainfall)",
  log_slope                  = "log(Slope)",
  log_hs                     = "log(Wave height)",
  gwetroot                   = "Antecedent soil moisture",
  island                     = "Island"
)

# ── LOAO CV helper for ranger ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RF has no random effects to exclude — predictions are already "population-level".
loao_cv_rf <- function(formula, data, response_col, num_trees = 500, seed = SEED) {
  aps   <- unique(data$ahupuaa)
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  n_skip <- 0L
  for (a in aps) {
    idx <- data$ahupuaa == a
    tr  <- data[!idx, ]; te <- data[idx, ]
    if (nrow(tr) < 30) { n_skip <- n_skip + 1L; next }
    m <- try(ranger(formula, data = tr, num.trees = num_trees,
                    seed = seed, importance = "none"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) { n_skip <- n_skip + 1L; next }
    preds[idx] <- predict(m, data = te)$predictions
  }
  if (n_skip > 0) message("LOAO RF: ", n_skip, " folds skipped")
  obs <- data[[response_col]]
  cv_metrics(obs, preds) |>
    mutate(n_folds = length(aps), n_skipped = n_skip, .before = n)
}

cat("Step 19 setup: predictor sets and loao_cv_rf defined.\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-datasets

# Build RF-ready datasets: select predictor + response columns, factor island.
# Use the same row sets as the GAM primary models (si_df, nox_primary, etc.).

si_rf_df <- si_df |>
  select(ahupuaa, island, all_of(si_rf_vars), log_Si) |>
  mutate(island = as.factor(island)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

nox_rf_df <- nox_primary |>
  select(ahupuaa, island, all_of(nox_rf_vars), log_NO3NO2) |>
  mutate(island = as.factor(island)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

po4_rf_df <- po4_primary |>
  select(ahupuaa, island, all_of(nox_rf_vars), log_PO4) |>
  mutate(island = as.factor(island)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

nh3_rf_df <- nh3_primary |>
  select(ahupuaa, island, all_of(nox_rf_vars), log_NH3) |>
  mutate(island = as.factor(island)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Model formulas
si_rf_form  <- as.formula(paste("log_Si ~",     paste(si_rf_vars,  collapse = " + ")))
nox_rf_form <- as.formula(paste("log_NO3NO2 ~", paste(nox_rf_vars, collapse = " + ")))
po4_rf_form <- as.formula(paste("log_PO4 ~",    paste(nox_rf_vars, collapse = " + ")))
nh3_rf_form <- as.formula(paste("log_NH3 ~",    paste(nox_rf_vars, collapse = " + ")))

cat("RF dataset sizes: Si =", nrow(si_rf_df),
    "| NOx =", nrow(nox_rf_df),
    "| PO4 =", nrow(po4_rf_df),
    "| NH4 =", nrow(nh3_rf_df), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-fit
#| cache: false

# Fit full RF models (with permutation importance) — file-cached.
# Delete the RDS to refit.
rf_full_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "step19_rf_full_models.rds")

if (file.exists(rf_full_path)) {
  rf_full <- readRDS(rf_full_path)
  cat("Loaded full RF models from cache.\n")
} else {
  set.seed(SEED)
  cat("Fitting full RF models (1000 trees each)...\n")
  rf_full <- list(
    Si  = ranger(si_rf_form,  data = si_rf_df,  num.trees = 1000,
                 importance = "permutation", seed = SEED),
    NOx = ranger(nox_rf_form, data = nox_rf_df, num.trees = 1000,
                 importance = "permutation", seed = SEED),
    PO4 = ranger(po4_rf_form, data = po4_rf_df, num.trees = 1000,
                 importance = "permutation", seed = SEED),
    NH4 = ranger(nh3_rf_form, data = nh3_rf_df, num.trees = 1000,
                 importance = "permutation", seed = SEED)
  )
  saveRDS(rf_full, rf_full_path)
  cat("Full RF models saved.\n")
}

# OOB R² is a good approximation of out-of-sample performance for RF
bind_rows(lapply(names(rf_full), \(nut) {
  tibble(Nutrient = nut,
         OOB_R2   = round(rf_full[[nut]]$r.squared, 3),
         OOB_RMSE = round(sqrt(rf_full[[nut]]$prediction.error), 3))
})) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Nutrient", "OOB R\u00b2", "OOB RMSE"),
               caption = "Step 19 \u2014 Random forest full-model out-of-bag performance.")
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-loao
#| cache: false

# LOAO CV for all four RF models — file-cached.
loao_rf_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "step19_rf_loao_cv.rds")

if (file.exists(loao_rf_path)) {

} else {

    NOx = loao_cv_rf(nox_rf_form, nox_rf_df, "log_NO3NO2", seed = SEED),
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-performance
#| fig-cap: "**Step 19 — RF vs GAM LOAO spatial CV R².** Each point is one nutrient. For NOx, the GAM LOAO baseline shown here uses the additive model (nox_M_full, R² = 0.300); the primary interaction model (nox_M_int, Step 17) achieves R² = 0.376, narrowing the RF advantage to ΔR² = 0.069. RF (with island as categorical predictor) outperforms the additive GAM for all four nutrients, reflecting the RF's ability to capture interaction and non-linear effects without explicit specification."

# RF vs GAM LOAO R² comparison
perf_df <- tibble(

perf_df |>

# Scatter: GAM R² vs RF R², labelled by nutrient
ggplot(perf_df, aes(GAM_LOAO, RF_LOAO, label = Nutrient)) +
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-importance
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "**Step 19 — Permutation variable importance for all four random forests.** Importance is the mean decrease in R² when a predictor's values are randomly permuted across out-of-bag samples (larger = more important). Colours mark predictor groups from the pre-registered conceptual framework. Variable importance reflects predictive contribution and must not be interpreted as causal attribution — correlated predictors share importance (e.g. island and cesspool exposure index are likely positively correlated)."

imp_df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(rf_full), \(nut) {
  imp <- rf_full[[nut]]$variable.importance
  tibble(Nutrient = nut, predictor = names(imp), importance = imp)
})) |>
  mutate(
    Nutrient  = factor(Nutrient, levels = c("Si", "NOx", "PO4", "NH4"),
                       labels = c("SiO\u2082", "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084")),
    group_lbl = rf_group[predictor],
    label     = rf_label[predictor],
    # Force negative importance to 0 for display (permutation can be slightly negative)
    importance = pmax(importance, 0)
  )

# Sort predictors within each facet by importance
imp_df |>
  group_by(Nutrient) |>
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(label, importance)) |>
  ggplot(aes(importance, label, fill = group_lbl)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Nutrient, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Terrestrial delivery" = "#1565C0",
               "Hydrologic forcing"   = "#00838F",
               "Watershed transport"  = "#2E7D32",
               "Anthropogenic"        = "#C62828",
               "Coastal dilution"     = "#6A1B9A",
               "Island"               = "grey55"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(x = "Permutation importance (mean decrease in R\u00b2)", y = NULL) +
  theme_kona_paper() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-pdp
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "**Step 19 — Partial dependence plots for the top continuous predictors.** Computed by varying one predictor across its 5–95th percentile range while averaging predictions over all observed values of other predictors (c-ICE marginalisation). Each panel shows the most important continuous predictor for that nutrient's RF, ordered by permutation importance rank. Shaded rug marks show the observed data distribution. Curves are on the log-response scale."

# Manual PDP: for each predictor × nutrient, vary the predictor on a grid
# and average RF predictions over all training rows
compute_pdp <- function(rf_model, data, var, n_grid = 40) {
  rng <- quantile(data[[var]], c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
  grid <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = n_grid)
  y    <- vapply(grid, function(v) {
    d_mod <- data; d_mod[[var]] <- v
    mean(predict(rf_model, data = d_mod)$predictions)
  }, numeric(1))
  tibble(x = grid, y = y, var = var)
}

# For each nutrient, identify top-2 continuous predictors by permutation importance
top_continuous <- imp_df |>
  filter(predictor != "island") |>
  group_by(Nutrient) |>
  slice_max(importance, n = 2) |>
  ungroup()

# Map back to original dataset/predictor-column names
nut_map <- list(
  "SiO\u2082"       = list(model = rf_full$Si,  data = si_rf_df),
  "NO\u2083+NO\u2082" = list(model = rf_full$NOx, data = nox_rf_df),
  "PO\u2084"        = list(model = rf_full$PO4, data = po4_rf_df),
  "NH\u2084"        = list(model = rf_full$NH4, data = nh3_rf_df)
)

pdp_all <- bind_rows(lapply(
  split(top_continuous, top_continuous$Nutrient),
  function(df) {
    nut   <- as.character(df$Nutrient[1])
    m_obj <- nut_map[[nut]]
    bind_rows(lapply(df$predictor, function(pvar) {
      compute_pdp(m_obj$model, m_obj$data, pvar) |>
        mutate(Nutrient = nut, group_lbl = rf_group[pvar],
               label    = rf_label[pvar])
    }))
  }
))

# Rug data (observed values for each predictor per nutrient)
rug_all <- bind_rows(lapply(
  split(top_continuous, top_continuous$Nutrient),
  function(df) {
    nut   <- as.character(df$Nutrient[1])
    m_obj <- nut_map[[nut]]
    bind_rows(lapply(df$predictor, function(pvar) {
      tibble(Nutrient = nut, label = rf_label[pvar],
             x = m_obj$data[[pvar]])
    }))
  }
))

ggplot(pdp_all, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_rug(data = rug_all, aes(x = x, y = NULL),
           sides = "b", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1565C0", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Nutrient + label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Predicted response (log scale, averaged)") +
  theme_kona_paper() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5))
```

```{r}
#| label: step19-rf-obs-pred
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "**Step 19 — RF LOAO CV: observed vs predicted.** Points represent samples from the held-out ahupuaʻa; predictions come from the RF trained on all other ahupuaʻa. The 1:1 line is solid grey. Colour encodes island. Unlike the LOIO test (Step 18B), island is a predictor in the RF so the model can use island-level context when predicting held-out ahupuaʻa."

# Reconstruct LOAO predictions (re-run or use saved loao_cv_rf with return_preds)
# Simpler: re-run with a thin wrapper that also returns predictions
get_loao_preds_rf <- function(formula, data, response_col, num_trees = 500, seed = SEED) {
  aps   <- unique(data$ahupuaa)
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  for (a in aps) {
    idx <- data$ahupuaa == a
    tr  <- data[!idx, ]; te <- data[idx, ]
    if (nrow(tr) < 30) next
    m <- try(ranger(formula, data = tr, num.trees = num_trees,
                    seed = seed, importance = "none"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) next
    preds[idx] <- predict(m, data = te)$predictions
  }
  tibble(obs = data[[response_col]], pred = preds,
         island = as.character(data$island),
         ahupuaa = data$ahupuaa)
}

# Cache the prediction vectors alongside LOAO metrics
loao_pred_path <- here("output", "model_objects", "step19_rf_loao_preds.rds")
if (file.exists(loao_pred_path)) {
  loao_pred_df <- readRDS(loao_pred_path)
} else {
  set.seed(SEED)
  cat("Reconstructing LOAO predictions for obs-vs-pred plot...\n")
  loao_pred_df <- bind_rows(
    get_loao_preds_rf(si_rf_form,  si_rf_df,  "log_Si",     seed = SEED) |>
      mutate(Nutrient = "SiO\u2082"),
    get_loao_preds_rf(nox_rf_form, nox_rf_df, "log_NO3NO2", seed = SEED) |>
      mutate(Nutrient = "NO\u2083+NO\u2082"),
    get_loao_preds_rf(po4_rf_form, po4_rf_df, "log_PO4",    seed = SEED) |>
      mutate(Nutrient = "PO\u2084"),
    get_loao_preds_rf(nh3_rf_form, nh3_rf_df, "log_NH3",    seed = SEED) |>
      mutate(Nutrient = "NH\u2084")
  )
  saveRDS(loao_pred_df, loao_pred_path)
}

# Reuse the island palette from global-constants (same encoding as data)
island_pal_rf <- island_pal

nut_order <- c("SiO\u2082", "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084")

loao_r2_labels <- loao_pred_df |>
  filter(!is.na(pred)) |>
  group_by(Nutrient) |>
  summarise(CV_R2 = round(1 - sum((obs-pred)^2)/sum((obs-mean(obs))^2), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Nutrient = factor(Nutrient, levels = nut_order))

ggplot(loao_pred_df |>
         filter(!is.na(pred)) |>
         mutate(Nutrient = factor(Nutrient, levels = nut_order)),
       aes(pred, obs, colour = island)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "loess", se = FALSE,
              colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = loao_r2_labels,
            aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf,
                label = paste0("CV R\u00b2 = ", CV_R2)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.4,
            size = 2.8, colour = "gray30") +
  facet_wrap(~ Nutrient, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = island_pal_rf, name = NULL,
                      na.value = "grey70") +
  labs(x = "Predicted (RF LOAO, log scale)",
       y = "Observed (log scale)") +
  theme_kona_paper() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

# Sensitivity Analyses {#sec-sensitivity}

> **Step 23.** Repeat key results under 11 analytical alternatives.
> Produce supplementary stability table.

## Si model — salinity diagnostic {#sec-sens-si-salinity}

Adding Salinity as a linear covariate to the Si connectivity model (`step11-si-salinity-sensitivity`)
is a diagnostic test, not a landscape predictor. It quantifies how much residual variance
and spatial autocorrelation reflects fine-scale freshwater/marine mixing that landscape-scale
predictors cannot resolve.

```{r}
#| label: step11-si-salinity-sensitivity

# ── Diagnostic sensitivity: add Salinity as a linear covariate ────────────────
# Salinity is a co-measured field variable — it partly reflects the freshwater
# fraction at the moment of sampling rather than a landscape driver. Including
# it here is diagnostic only: we use it to quantify how much of the residual
# variance and spatial autocorrelation is attributable to local
# freshwater/marine mixing that landscape predictors cannot resolve.
# This model is NOT used for inference in the main analysis.
M_int_sal <- gam(
  log_Si ~ te(log_dist_m, log_slope, bs = "tp", k = 6) +
           s(log_chirps, bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           s(log_ksat,   bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           gwetroot +
           s(log_hs,     bs = "tp", k = 8) +
           Salinity +                         # diagnostic only — not a landscape predictor
           s(island_f,  bs = "re") +
           s(ahupuaa_f, bs = "re") +
           s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs = "tp", k = 25),
  data = si_df, method = "REML"
)

diag_compare <- tibble(
  model         = c(best_label, paste0(best_label, " + Salinity")),
  dev_expl_pct  = c(round(summary(M_int)$dev.expl    * 100, 1),
                    round(summary(M_int_sal)$dev.expl * 100, 1)),
  adj_r2        = c(round(summary(M_int)$r.sq,    3),
                    round(summary(M_int_sal)$r.sq, 3)),
  resid_morans  = c(resid_morans(best_model,  si_sf_model)$morans_I,
                    resid_morans(M_int_sal, si_sf_model)$morans_I),
  resid_p       = c(resid_morans(best_model,  si_sf_model)$p_value,
                    resid_morans(M_int_sal, si_sf_model)$p_value)
)

diag_compare |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Model", "Dev. expl. (%)", "Adj-R²",
                  "Residual Moran's I", "p-value"),
    caption   = paste(
      "Salinity diagnostic: adding Salinity as a linear term absorbs ~10 percentage",
      "points of additional deviance and reduces residual Moran's I,",
      "confirming that residual spatial structure in",
      best_label,
      "reflects local freshwater/marine mixing at the time of sampling —",
      "a fine-scale hydrodynamic signal irreducible by watershed-scale landscape",
      "predictors. The landscape model is not misspecified; log(Si) in Step 12",
      "serves as an empirical proxy for this mixing ratio within the NO3+NO2 model."
    )
  )

cat("\nSalinity slope (log-Si per PSU):",
    round(coef(M_int_sal)["Salinity"], 4),
    "— each 1-PSU increase in salinity associated with",
    round(abs(coef(M_int_sal)["Salinity"]) * 100, 1),
    "% lower Si on the log scale.\n")

saveRDS(M_int_sal, here("output", "model_objects", "si_M_int_sal_diagnostic.rds"))
```

## Cesspool metric choice {#sec-sens-cesspool}

The three-island submodels (Steps 12–14; Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi) represent wastewater with
two ahupuaʻa- and sample-level metrics: cesspool **density** (ahupuaʻa cesspools km⁻²) and
**distance to the nearest** cesspool. Two sample-level **buffer counts** — cesspools within
500 m and within 1 km — are an alternative that captures *local* cesspool abundance
directly. On the three-island subset the two buffers are strongly correlated (Spearman
ρ ≈ 0.83) so they enter one at a time; notably, buffer counts are nearly orthogonal to
ahupuaʻa density (ρ ≈ 0.26) but strongly track distance-to-nearest (ρ ≈ −0.89) — i.e. they
are an alternative *local-proximity* metric, not a restatement of density. Buffer counts
now have complete sample-level coverage on Oʻahu, Maui, and Molokaʻi (Molokaʻi from the
DOH OSDS 2010 inventory; see comparability caveat, §Step 12); Lānaʻi buffer counts are
correctly 0 (no on-island cesspools in the HCPT layer) but density/distance remain `NA`
there. To isolate the effect of the metric choice, each specification below is fit on the
**same rows** as the main submodel.

```{r}
#| label: step23-cesspool-metric-sensitivity
#| cache: true

# Refit each nutrient submodel on identical three-island rows, swapping the cesspool
# block: (density + distance) vs n within 500 m vs n within 1 km. Counts are log1p'd;
# all predictors z-standardized within each fit. log_SiO2 is dropped when Si is the
# response (it would otherwise be response and predictor).
cess_base <- c("log_SiO2", "chirps_storm_cumulative_mm", "log_dist_stream_m",
               "mean_slope_deg", "log_ksat", "pct_agriculture", "pct_impervious",
               "log_dist_npdes_m", "fetch_mean_km", "hs_mean_m")
cess_re_3isl   <- "s(island_f, bs='re') + s(ahupuaa_f, bs='re') + s(utm_x_km, utm_y_km, bs='tp', k=25)"

fit_cess_specs <- function(resp) {
  bdlcol <- paste0("bdl_", resp)
  bv <- if (resp == "SiO2") setdiff(cess_base, "log_SiO2") else cess_base
  d <- chem_master |>
    filter(island %in% c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i"),
           !is.na(cesspool_density_per_km2), !is.na(dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m),
           !is.na(n_cess_500m), !is.na(n_cess_1km),
           !is.na(.data[[resp]]), !.data[[bdlcol]], !bdl_SiO2) |>
    left_join(sp_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(sample_id, utm_x, utm_y), by = "sample_id") |>
    mutate(
      y = log(.data[[resp]]), log_SiO2 = log(SiO2),
      log_dist_stream_m = log(dist_to_stream_mouth_m + 1), log_ksat = log(mean_ksat_um_s + 1),
      log_dist_npdes_m = log(dist_to_nearest_npdes_m + 1),
      log_cesspool_density = log(cesspool_density_per_km2 + 1),
      log_dist_cesspool_m = log(dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m + 1),
      log_n500 = log1p(n_cess_500m), log_n1km = log1p(n_cess_1km),
      island_f = factor(island), ahupuaa_f = factor(ahupuaa),
      utm_x_km = utm_x / 1000, utm_y_km = utm_y / 1000
    ) |>
    filter(if_all(all_of(c("y", bv)), ~ !is.na(.)), !is.na(utm_x_km))

  specs <- list("Density + distance (main)" = c("log_cesspool_density", "log_dist_cesspool_m"),
                "n within 500 m" = "log_n500", "n within 1 km" = "log_n1km")
  imap_dfr(specs, function(cv, nm) {
    allv <- c(bv, cv)
    dd <- d |> mutate(across(all_of(allv), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x)), .names = "z_{.col}"))
    m  <- gam(as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(paste0("z_", allv), collapse = " + "), "+", cess_re_3isl)),
              data = dd, method = "REML")
    coef_ci(m, nm) |> filter(term %in% paste0("z_", cv)) |>
      mutate(nutrient = resp, n = nrow(dd))
  })
}

cess_sens <- map_dfr(c("NO3NO2", "PO4", "NH3", "SiO2"), fit_cess_specs)

metric_lab <- c(log_cesspool_density = "Cesspool density", log_dist_cesspool_m = "Dist to nearest",
                log_n500 = "n within 500 m", log_n1km = "n within 1 km")
nut_lab    <- c(NO3NO2 = "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", PO4 = "PO\u2084", NH3 = "NH\u2084", SiO2 = "SiO\u2082")

cess_sens |>
  transmute(
    Nutrient      = factor(nut_lab[nutrient], levels = c("SiO\u2082", "NO\u2083+NO\u2082", "PO\u2084", "NH\u2084")),
    Specification = model,
    Metric        = metric_lab[str_remove(term, "z_")],
    std_beta      = round(est, 3),
    ci95          = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lwr, upr),
    p             = signif(p, 2),
    n
  ) |>
  arrange(Nutrient, Specification) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Nutrient", "Specification", "Metric", "Std. \u03b2", "95% CI", "p", "n"),
    caption = "Table S. Cesspool-metric sensitivity (three-island: Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi, identical rows per nutrient). Standardized coefficient for each cesspool metric under three specifications; distance-to-nearest and buffer counts are alternative local-proximity metrics, density is ahupuaʻa-scale.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-important}
**The cesspool signal is metric-dependent — and the choice changes which nutrient
responds.** For **NO₃+NO₂**, the local buffer counts are significant positive
predictors (n within 500 m: β ≈ 0.18; within 1 km: β ≈ 0.17; both 95% CIs exclude zero)
even though ahupuaʻa density and distance-to-nearest were not — a local cesspool signal
that the ahupuaʻa-average density metric misses. **PO₄** shows a weak positive effect of
the 1 km count only (β ≈ 0.09). **NH₄**, by contrast, responds to ahupuaʻa **density**
(β ≈ 0.20) but *not* to buffer counts. **Si** responds only to distance-to-nearest
(negative), consistent with a connectivity confound rather than a source signal. The
robust reading is that cesspool associations are real but modest and depend on the
spatial scale of the metric: local counts capture near-field NO₃+NO₂ enrichment, whereas
ahupuaʻa density better tracks NH₄. This reinforces treating the cesspool result as
correlational and scale-sensitive rather than a single clean "wastewater effect."
:::
